title: fix(2d): Pass starts at (Auto/Inside/Outside) for 2D Pocket
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first).

## What changed

2D Pocket gets the shared "Pass starts at" option of #3316 (Auto / Inside / Outside).

- `OpParams::Pocket` gets the field `pass_start: machining2d::PassStart`. This is the same type as on 2D Offset. There is no new type.
- The project file uses the same key, `pass_start`. The file never writes `auto`. Files without the key read as Auto.
- The Passes tab of 2D Pocket shows the same row, `Pass starts at` (`pass_start_row`).
- MCP uses the same generic `edit_operation` door. Undo goes through `EditOperationParams`.
- The digest writes the value only off Auto. The byte pair is now one helper, `digest::write_pass_start`. 2D Offset and 2D Pocket both use it.
- The generator calls `pocket_started` (from #3353) instead of `pocket_entered_with_relief`. On Auto, the two functions are byte-identical.
- Waterline and Offset rings read the value through the #3316 ring law (`PassStart::rank`).
- Zigzag rows have no inside or outside. With Inside or Outside, the planner adds the path note `PASS_START_ZIGZAG_NOTE`.
- Rest machining keeps its own order of the rest areas. With Inside or Outside, the generator adds the path note `PASS_START_REST_NOTE`.
- About 40 test struct literals get `pass_start: Default::default()`. This is a mechanical change.
- The site guide (2D Pocket) gets a row and a paragraph.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3354-pocket-pass-start.md`.

## Cause

2D Pocket had no pass-order choice. With an Outside containment, the ring strategies cut each level core-first. The first ring was then a full slot in the stock. This is the #3316 defect on the pocket kind.

## Tests

The pins (`crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs`, `fig8.step`, EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, the #3316 heights):

- `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`: Waterline and Offset rings. The first ring of each level is at least one tool radius outside the stock. The last ring is on the part wall.
- `fig8_pocket_inside_starts_each_level_on_the_part_wall`
- `fig8_pocket_auto_keeps_the_core_first_order`: Auto has no note and no stock-edge start.
- `fig8_zigzag_pocket_says_pass_start_is_not_used`
- `fig8_rest_pocket_says_pass_start_is_not_used`
- `pocket_pass_start_rides_mcp_undo_and_the_file`: an unknown word is refused, `auto` is not written, undo restores the value, and the file round-trips.
- `operation::rest_op_tests::pass_start_moves_the_pocket_stamp_only_off_auto` (app lib)
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::the_pocket_passes_tab_offers_pass_start_and_shows_the_draft` (ui lib)

Mutation checks. I removed each guard, ran its pin, and put the guard back. Each pin went red and then green again:

- generator call back to `pocket_entered_with_relief`: the Outside, Inside and Zigzag pins went red.
- Zigzag note removed: the Zigzag pin went red.
- file DTO writes Auto always: the MCP and file pin went red.
- digest bytes removed: the stamp pin went red.
- rest note removed: the rest pin went red.
- UI row removed: the UI pin went red.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-3353` planned 743 steps, because any change in `crates/app/src` selects every app suite. That run hit its time limit, so I ran a targeted set instead.
- Green: app lib, motion lib and ui lib.
- Green: every test binary that this PR edits (35 app suites and `edge_loop_pick`).
- Green: `offset_pass_start`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `conformance`, `whole_model_pocket`, `mcp_dxf` and `do_not_touch`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. Auto is byte-identical.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate (743 steps) did not complete. See the Gate list above for what ran.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row still says "2D Offset" only. The edit needed a permission that this headless run did not have. A follow-up can add "or a 2D Pocket" and the note about Zigzag and rest.
- Pass start with "Do not touch" (`pocket_avoid_started`) is not wired for 2D Pocket. 2D Pocket does not use the avoid planner.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #3353 (the shared type, key, row and ring law). This PR changes one line of #3353 in `params/mill2d.rs`, because the Offset2D digest now uses the shared helper. The bytes are the same.
- Other open PRs touch `generate.rs`, `project/params.rs` and `params_impl.rs` (#3283, #3251, #3103, #3058, #2890, #2831) and `mill2d_page.rs` (#2817, #2890). They change different functions or arms. The PR that merges second does the refresh.

Changelog: 2D Pocket: new "Pass starts at" option (Auto / Inside / Outside) on the Passes tab, in MCP and in the project file; Outside starts each ring level at the outer edge, so an Outside containment no longer slots the stock.

Fixes #3354

title: fix(trace): enforce protected face and edge clearance
body:
Stacked on #3352. The parent PR routes viewport clicks to an armed Boundary row.

Trace now accepts protected faces and edges. Generation checks the full tool along the selected line, including links and plunges. If a move cannot keep the requested clearance, generation refuses it and names the protected item. The post gate checks current protected geometry again. A Trace without protected items keeps its original moves.

**Verification on `abed47739`**

- `trace_protects_the_full_sweep_between_clear_endpoints` failed on the parent when MCP refused protected items on Trace. It passes on this head.
- The test places a protected face between two clear endpoints. The holder reaches it at a distance of 14.9 mm with a 15 mm clearance envelope. The shank reaches it at 6.9 mm with a 7 mm envelope. The clear case keeps the original moves. A refused path writes no NC file.
- `tilted_trace_refuses_a_protected_face_in_its_work_plane` passes.
- `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click` passes with actual viewport clicks.
- All 40 tests passed in the app suites `area_controls`, `do_not_touch`, `do_not_touch_project`, `engrave_law`, and `mill2d_b`. All six UI tests selected by `do_not_touch` passed. Clippy passed for all targets in the app and UI crates with warnings denied.

All 203 release-mode test steps selected by the heavy gate completed. The 26-step run covered the suites with ignored tests, the library, binary and doc steps, and the registered expected failures for #1950 and #2849. The other 177 steps also passed. The gate reported zero unexpected failures.

The heavy plan also lists one compile-only step for all 644 app integration targets. I built the reached targets separately on this host to fit the available disk. This PR stays in draft. The change was not exercised on a physical machine.

Changelog: Trace accepts protected faces and edges and refuses a path that cannot keep the full tool clear.

Effort: high

Fixes #3348

title: fix(ui): keep Post dialog checkboxes clear of the scroll bar; adapt two Adaptive tests
body:
Main is red in the post-merge gate. This PR makes the three red tests green.

## Test 1: Post dialog (guilty merge: PR #3307, 887d8da2a)

`egui_app::post_dialog_tests::desktop_post_command_opens_dialog_and_applies_declared_script_options_undoably`

```
panicked at crates\ui\src\egui_app\post_dialog_tests.rs:69:5:
assertion `left == right` failed: clicking Write tool list at [[551.0 514.0] - [569.0 532.0]] must toggle draft value
  left: Some(Bool(false))
 right: Some(Bool(true))
```

Cause (product defect):
- PR #3307 adds the Fanuc row "Manual Guide i blank (G1902 / G1900)".
- With this row, the options are higher than the scroll area at a 900 px window. egui shows its floating vertical scroll bar.
- The bar lies over the right edge of the content, where `check_row` puts the checkbox. The click goes to the bar, not to the checkbox. A user has the same problem.
- Proof: at a 1400 px window (no scroll bar) the test passes, with the same checkbox rect.

Change: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog.rs` keeps a right gutter in the scroll content, as wide as the scroll bar (`bar_width + bar_inner_margin + bar_outer_margin`). The test keeps its 900 px window. It now also pins the new `manualGuideBlank` row: listed, off by default, toggles, is applied in the same undo step, and Ctrl+Z removes it.

## Tests 2 and 3: Adaptive fallback warning (guilty merge: PR #3108, 92935735e)

```
blind_slot_pocket_family_cuts_from_end_wall_to_stock_edge
panicked at crates\app\tests\blind_slot.rs:142:13:
assertion `left == right` failed: Adaptive2D
  left: 1
 right: 0
```

```
adaptive2d_spiral_and_offset2d_support_relief_while_trochoidal_and_do_not_touch_refuse
panicked at crates\app\tests\corner_relief_safety.rs:177:5:
adaptive2d dogbone verify must be silent: [StrategyFallback { at: 2, areas: 1 }]
```

Cause (test only): PR #3108 makes an Adaptive fallback to the Offset rings an advisory `StrategyFallback` warning. These two tests still expected zero warnings. The only warning is `StrategyFallback`, and its `areas` agrees with `machining2d::rings_fallbacks(&notes)`. The product is correct.

Change: the two assertions use the pattern of #3108 (`shoulder_adaptive.rs`): the warning count is 1 only when the notes show a fallback; each warning must be `StrategyFallback` with the same area count and must not block the post. All other checks stay.

## Results (debug, worktree on origin/main 62353ac75)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --exact egui_app::post_dialog_tests::desktop_post_command_opens_dialog_and_applies_declared_script_options_undoably`: ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: `test result: ok. 1427 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test blind_slot --test corner_relief_safety`: `4 passed` and `3 passed`, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test blind_slot --test corner_relief_safety -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches `app heavy: blind_slot` and `app heavy: corner_relief_safety`. The two files have no `#[ignore]` test, so the lanes are empty. Not run.

## Not exercised
- The Setup -> Post page (`post_script_options::section`) also draws `check_row` rows. I did not examine it for the same scroll bar overlap.
- No snapshot PNG changes. The look of the Post dialog changes by the gutter width at the right edge.

## Screenshots
The pictures are headless renders of the test harness (`egui_kittest`) at a 900 px window. They show the Post dialog with the built-in Fanuc post. No application window was started.
The images are on the images-only `screenshots` branch (commit `308d2de02`). No image is on this PR branch.

Before: main `62353ac75`. The scroll bar lies over the checkboxes and the fields at the right edge of the rows.

![Before: scroll bar over the right edge of the rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/308d2de02c5a62995db77f43ec49d75529abb2d6/pr-3388/post-dialog-before.png)

After: this PR head `1fc20d3d0`. The rows keep a gap on the right. The checkboxes are clear of the scroll bar.

![After: checkboxes clear of the scroll bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/308d2de02c5a62995db77f43ec49d75529abb2d6/pr-3388/post-dialog-after.png)

title: fix(2d): Face says it has no pass order on the Pass starts at row
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first).

## What changed

Face now shows the shared "Pass starts at" row on its Passes tab. The row is held at Auto and is disabled. A line under it, in view, says why: Face rows run edge to edge, so there is no inside or outside order.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pass_start_row.rs`: new `no_pass_order_row` and the text `FACE_NO_PASS_ORDER`. The row uses the same label and combo as 2D Offset.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mill2d_page.rs`: the Face Passes tab draws that row.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`: `edit_operation` with `pass_start` on a Face is refused by name. The message says that Face has no pass order and that its rows run edge to edge. Before, the refusal was the generic "unknown field". Every word is refused, `auto` too, because Face has no such field.
- `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`: one row in the Face table.
- `docs/decisions/3356-face-pass-start.md`: the decision.

The issue permits this result: "If Face has no pass order, its row says so by name, and the issue records why."

## Cause

Face cuts serpentine rows from the low Y edge to the high Y edge (`face_over`, `band`). The first row and the last row are both at an edge. There are no rings. An Inside or Outside order has no meaning for these rows. A centre-out order would add a lift and a link through clearance for each row, with no machining gain. So Face gets no `pass_start` field. A field that changes nothing would mislead the user.

## Tests

- `camcraft-app` `face_pass_start::mcp_refuses_pass_start_on_face_by_the_row_order`: `outside`, `inside` and `auto` are refused with the reason, and the job does not change. Red before the fix: the message was `unknown field pass_start - a face operation has no field "pass_start"`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::pass_start::the_face_passes_tab_says_it_has_no_pass_order`: one `Pass starts at` row, one disabled combo that shows Auto, and the reason in view. Red before the fix: no row (0, expected 1).
- `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`: the Face Passes row list now has `Pass starts at` (an expected change).

Mutation checks (old file put back from `base-3353`, pin run, file restored):
- `mcp/edit.rs` old: the MCP pin is red. Restored: green.
- `mill2d_page.rs` old: the UI pin is red. Restored: green.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-3353` (the #3353 head): 30 steps, 0 failed. It ran app lib, `face_pass_start`, `mcp_enum_patch` and the other touched app suites, and ui lib and the touched ui suites. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. Face output does not change: the planner is not touched.

## Not exercised

- No GUI screenshot was taken.
- The heavy lanes were not run. The diff does not touch `motion` or any generator.
- A project file with a `pass_start` key on a Face is not tested. Face writes no such key. Serde ignores an unknown key on load, as it did before.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for this refusal is not added. The edit of `.claude/skills/` was blocked in this session. A follow-up can add one sentence to the Pass starts at row.

## Overlaps

- #3353: the stack base (`pass_start_row.rs`, `mcp/edit.rs`, `mill2d_page.rs`, `tests.rs`, the guide).
- #3251: changes other lines of `patched()` in `mcp/edit.rs` (the back-check loop). This PR adds a guard before the merge loop. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2890 and #2817: change other arms of `fields()` in `mill2d_page.rs`. Not the Face arm.
- Many open PRs change `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`. This PR changes one line of the Face table.

Changelog: Face: the Passes tab shows "Pass starts at" as not used, with the reason (Face rows run edge to edge); MCP refuses pass_start on a Face by that reason.

Fixes #3356

title: fix(boundary): separate inside and outside boundary offsets
body:
## What changed

- `AreaControls` has a new field `outer_offset`. It moves only the outer side of an open boundary (the stock side). `offset` now moves only the picked line, or the whole area when there is no open boundary.
- The area law (`operation::boundary::resolve`, step 2) reads the two values. When they are equal, it runs the old code path exactly. When they differ on an open boundary, `boundary_turn::grow_apart` grows the kept side by the larger value and clips it to the stock reach grown by `outer_offset`. The far side, shrunk by `offset`, cuts the picked line as before.
- The Boundary group has two rows: "Inside boundary offset" and "Outside boundary offset". Each row has its own hint. Both start at 0. The summary says how the outer side moves. It gives a notice when an outside offset has no open boundary to act on.
- The project file has an optional `outer_offset` key in `area`. An absent key means "the same as `offset`". An old file loads its one offset into both values and saves the same bytes. There is no version bump.
- The stamp hashes `outer_offset` only when it differs from `offset`. The stamp of an old operation does not change.
- MCP: `set_operation_area` takes `outer_offset`, and the area view shows it. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the tool description name it.

## Cause

The law had one offset step. It grew the kept side of an open boundary by `offset` and shrank the far side by the same value. The one value moved the picked line and the stock line together. A negative value to cut less air also moved the area away from the picked edge.

## Tests

New pins:
- `crates/app/tests/area_outer_offset.rs`
  - `a_negative_outer_offset_pulls_in_the_stock_side_and_keeps_the_picked_edge`: side B of an open boundary on the block's north edge, stock 70 mm, tool R 5. With outer -10 and picked 0, the region edge stays on the chain (y 20) and the outer edge moves from +-45 to +-35. The Pocket feed length drops from 605.8 mm to 315.8 mm. The test also checks the picked offset alone, and a positive picked offset with a negative outer offset.
  - `one_value_in_both_offsets_is_the_old_law`: equal values -2 move both lines (y 22 and 43). A closed area ignores the outer offset.
  - `an_old_project_offset_loads_into_both_and_saves_the_same_bytes`: the migration. A file with one `offset` key loads into both values, and save-load-save gives the same bytes. Different values round-trip, and an outer offset of 0 is written.
  - `the_outer_offset_rides_the_door_and_the_undo`: one undoable `EditOperationParams` step. The door refuses a non-finite value.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary_offset_tests.rs`
  - `the_boundary_group_has_an_inside_and_an_outside_offset_row`: labels, hints, default 0, an edit of the outside row changes only `outer_offset`, Apply commits it, and undo restores it.
  - `the_summary_says_an_outside_offset_without_an_open_boundary_does_nothing`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_pick.rs`: `set_operation_area` sets and shows `outer_offset`, and undo resets it.

Red before the fix: the pin did not compile on upstream/main (no field `outer_offset`). With the field and the old law, it failed: `the outer edge moves in: -45 45 45`.

Mutations (each put back, pin run, then restored and green again):
- Old law in step 2 (guard off): red, `the outer edge moves in: -45 45 45`.
- `grow_apart` grows by `outer` only: red, `the picked edge stays on the chain: 30`.
- DTO loads an absent key as 0: red, `the one offset loads into both`.
- Door without `dist(outer_offset)`: red, `a non-finite outer offset is refused`.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 46 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1426 passed.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`, 205 app steps): 0 failed, wall 48.4 min.

Expected-change test: `egui_app::tests::do_not_touch::geometry_boundaries_shows_do_not_touch_controls_rows_and_viewport_marks` failed because the new row moved the last remove button below the 1100 px harness. The harness is now 1200 px tall. The assertions did not change.

## Goldens moved

None. Equal offsets run the old code path, so no golden `.cl` or `.nc` changed.

## Not exercised

- The Face family and a closed ring as the open boundary with two different offsets. They use the same `grow_apart` step, but no test pins them.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill text still lists the old `area` keys. It is a process file, and this PR does not change it. The tool schema describes the new key.
- `crates/app/src/operation/boundary.rs` grows from 400 to 406 lines. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs` was 437 lines before and is 439 now.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/3338-outer-boundary-offset.md`. The issue asked for a project-file version bump. This PR uses an optional key instead: an old file loads into both values and saves the same bytes, so a bump gives no gain.

## Overlaps

- #3304 (draft i18n) wraps strings in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs` and `crates/ui/src/boundary_summary.rs`. It touches the same files, but a different change (string wrapping). The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #3283 and #3058 (draft feats) touch `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs`. They change the kind list in `area_unsupported`, a different function. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Effort: high

Changelog: Boundary settings have separate inside and outside offsets. The outside offset moves only the stock side of an open boundary, so less air is cut and the picked edge stays in place. An old project keeps its output.

Fixes #3338

title: test(app): bench the playback cost on the fig8 2D Offset and a 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

One new test file: `crates/app/tests/stock_play_cost_bench.rs` (300 lines). No product code changes.

The file has three `#[ignore]`d tests in the heavy lane (playback perf bench). They print readings and assert no wall time:

- `playback_cost_on_the_fig8_2d_offset`
- `playback_cost_on_the_3d_pocket`
- `playback_cost_against_the_cell_count` (the two fixtures at 1/4 and 1/2 of `DEFAULT_TEXELS`)

## What the bench measures

Each test builds the document through the commands, then walks the program as a playing worker does:

1. A chunk of moves with `FieldPlay::seek`. The chunk law is the law of the worker (first chunk 64, 15 ms target, 1..1024).
2. One publication: `take_dirty`, `view`, then `pack_cut_patch`, or `pack_cut` when the patch is not smaller than the layer.
3. On each 8th chunk, one more whole-layer `pack_cut` (the cost of a repack on the render thread).

It prints the lattice dims and the cell, the moves, ms for each chunk and each move, the `CutStats` counters for each move, ms for each pack, and the share of each part in one publication. A debug walk stops after 90 s and prints how far it went.

The fig8 stock is my choice: 100 x 140 x 22 mm, centred on the part (the part box plus about 7.5 mm on each side). The Pocket is the `pocket3d_hsm.rs` setup with the default OffsetRings plan.

## Readings

Machine: Intel Core i9-10980XE, 18 cores, 36 threads. Base: `origin/main` b6a3e7c6b. Median of three runs, `DEFAULT_TEXELS`.

| Reading | fig8 release | fig8 debug | Pocket release | Pocket debug |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Texels per layer, cell | 516,780, 1.055 mm | same | 470,000, 0.796 mm | same |
| Moves (walked) | 2,670 (2,670) | 2,670 (1,823) | 4,658 (4,658) | 4,658 (2,904) |
| Cut, ms for each move | 15.12 | 32.95 | 5.53 | 19.58 |
| `pack_cut_patch`, ms | 0.19 | 1.37 | 0.16 | 1.25 |
| `pack_cut` whole layer, ms | 14.07 | 165.4 | 9.73 | 132.1 |
| Cut share of a publication | 99 % | 97 % | 99 % | 96 % |

The full table, the cell-count sweep and the facts are in the comment on #3336.

## How to run

`cargo test -p camcraft-app --release --test stock_play_cost_bench -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`

## Tests and gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (6 jobs): green. Its plan has the one step `app suites: stock_play_cost_bench` (no test runs: all three are ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test stock_play_cost_bench -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The three ignored tests: three runs in release, all pass. The two default tests: three runs in debug, all pass.

## Not exercised

- The GPU upload (`write_cut`, `write_cut_patch`) and the march. The bench has no GPU device. It prints the bytes only.
- The UI thread (`ensure_field_view`). `crates/ui/src/play_bench_tests.rs` measures it.
- The partial move (`seek_to` with a fraction) and the precalc of keyframes.
- Other machines and the Linux cut runner.

Effort: medium

Changelog: none

Refs #3336

Fixes #3365

title: docs(process): merge-ready and needs-rework never coexist
body:
## What changed
The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

New rule, written with the same words in each place:
- `merge-ready` and `needs-rework` are never on the same PR.
- The person or agent that sets one removes the other in the same `gh pr edit` call, with one comment that says why.
- If two collaborators disagree on the same head, `needs-rework` stays and `merge-ready` is removed. An open change request wins. The comment goes to the collaborator who set `merge-ready`.
- `/merge-ready` never offers a PR with `needs-rework`.
- `conflicts` stays an add-alongside label.

Files:
- `AGENTS.md`: rule "Only collaborators' reviews count" (the disagreement item is replaced by three items) and one line below the "Review labels" table.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: the disagreement paragraph is replaced by the rule. A PR with `needs-rework` is not offered.
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md`: the label steps say "in the same `gh pr edit` call". The disagreement paragraph is replaced by the rule.
- `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`: step 8 sets one label and removes the other in one call.
- `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md`: the DELTA verdict `needs-rework` removes `merge-ready` in the same call.

No file under `xtask/` pins the old text. No test changes.

## Not exercised
No build and no test run. This is a text change in process files.

title: fix(picks): one shared start / exit pick mechanism for every kind
body:
## What changed

- New `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md`. It records each answer of #3324: the choice, the reason and the dropped options. The issue names this path, so the file uses it in place of `3324-<slug>.md`.
- New shared type `camcraft_motion::path_picks`: `PathPicks { start, exit }` of `PathPick { xy, z }`, and `PickRole`. The type holds lists. `PathPicks::refusal` refuses a second pick of one role by name. It also refuses a coordinate that is not finite or is more than 1 km from the origin.
- New `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`:
  - `PickCapability` (`Ring`, `Region`, `HoleOrder`, `Ends`, `Raster`, `Threading`, `NotTaken(reason)`).
  - `KindInfo::pick()`, an exhaustive match on `OpType`. 2D Contour is `Ring`. Wire Contour is `Threading`. Probe is `NotTaken` ("cuts no path"). Every other kind is `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` until its family slice of #1448 ships.
  - `OpParams::path_picks()`, one accessor for every kind. It reads `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point` and `WireContourOp.start`.
  - `OpParams::pick_refusal()`. `named_refusal` now calls it in place of the old hard-coded match.
- MCP: the `params` description of `edit_operation` names `links.approach.start_point` and `links.approach.exit_point` and the kinds that take them. Each kind of `list_operation_types` has a `start_exit` answer (`start`, `exit`, and `field` or `why_not`).
- UI: every operation page draws the Start point and Exit point groups. A kind that does not take a pick shows one line in each group: "Not taken - <reason>". The line is on the Lead in / Lead out tab, or on Geometry when the kind has no lead tab. The contour keeps its editable rows.

## Cause

The maintainer could not see a start or exit point on the 2D Offset (#1448, 2026-11-22). Only the closed 2D Contour took a pick. The refusal on other kinds did not name the kind. No page said that the pick is not taken. The family slices of #1448 had no shared mechanism.

## Message change

The refusal of a pick on a kind that does not take it was:
`a start point is taken only by the 2D contour so far - clear it on this operation`.
It is now, for example:
`2D Offset: a start point is not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships; clear it on this operation`.
The tilted contour refusal does not change.

## Tests

Pins:
- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs` (new, 4 tests):
  - `a_pick_on_a_kind_that_does_not_take_it_names_the_kind_and_the_reason`
  - `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`
  - `path_picks_reads_the_contour_pick_and_the_wire_start`
  - `the_mcp_doors_name_the_pick_fields_and_the_kinds_that_take_them`
- `egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::kinds_without_a_picked_start_say_so_by_name`. It was `kinds_without_a_picked_start_draw_neither_group`. The expected behaviour changed on purpose. It now also covers the 2D Offset.

Red before the fix: the two MCP tests ran on unchanged code and failed. The refusal said "taken only by the 2D contour so far" with no kind name. The schema said only "Fields to change". The other two tests use the new API.

Mutations:
- `sane.rs` from `upstream/main`: `a_pick_on_a_kind_that_does_not_take_it_names_the_kind_and_the_reason` is red. Restored: green.
- The `not_taken_groups` call in `op_page.rs` removed: `kinds_without_a_picked_start_say_so_by_name` is red. Restored: green.

Unchanged and green: `contour_start_point` (8 tests, with the golden `contour_start_point.cl`), and the start / exit UI tests (`start_exit_rows`, `start_exit_pick`, `start_exit_viewport`).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 347 steps, and 346 passed. The one red step was `machine::a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door`. Upstream fixed that test in 80e8891e0 after the branch point (the router kind of #3279). After a merge of `upstream/main`, these pass: `machine` (33), `start_exit_shared` (4), `contour_start_point` (8) and the UI `start_exit` tests (13).
Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The storage move to one operation-level `picks` key, and the load tests of the old `links.approach.start_point` key and the old wire `start` key. They are in #3339. The decision file says why: the move changes every path variant, and more than ten open PRs change `wire_edm.rs` / `wire_edm_dto.rs`.
- The shared ring helpers (`nearest_on_ring`, `reach`, `lead_held`) do not move yet. They move with the first family slice that calls them.
- The viewport snap for `Region`, `HoleOrder`, `Ends` and `Raster`. No kind has these capabilities yet.
- No planner changes. The family sub-issues of #1448 do that.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch nearby code. No open PR changes the same function. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3283, #3251, #3103, #3058, #2890 and #2831 change `kinds.rs`. This PR does not change `kinds.rs`. A PR that adds an `OpType` must add an arm to `KindInfo::pick()` in `pick_kinds.rs`. The match is exhaustive on purpose.
- #3251 changes `mcp/edit.rs`. This PR does not change it.
- #3304 changes `approach_page.rs`. This PR does not change it.

Changelog: Every operation page shows the Start point and Exit point groups; a kind that does not take a pick yet says so by name, the refusal of such a pick names the kind, and MCP `edit_operation` / `list_operation_types` say which kinds take a pick.

Effort: max

Fixes #3324

title: fix(gpu): headless compute seam with probe, CPU fallback and a parity-tested binning kernel
body:
## What changed

- A new crate `crates/gpu` (`camcraft-gpu`) holds the headless GPU compute seam.
  - `adapter.rs`: the windowless device policy. The software adapter comes first, then the hardware adapter (#615). This code moved down from `camcraft-ui`'s `headless_gpu.rs`.
  - `probe.rs`: the capability probe. It reads `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS` and the device limits. A WebGL2 or GL adapter below ES 3.1 gives "no compute" by name.
  - `shared.rs`: one device for each process (`OnceLock`). The first request makes it. A device-lost callback marks it lost. After that, the CPU path runs for the rest of the process.
  - `switch.rs`: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` (also `0`, `false`, `no`) turns GPU compute off. The fallback reason is logged one time for each process.
  - `binning.rs`, `binning_gpu.rs`, `binning.wgsl`: the first kernel, conservative facet binning. The input is facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` and a margin. The output is one facet list for each cell.
- Each entry returns `Result`. An `Err` names the reason: no adapter, no compute, the switch is off, a lost device, a buffer past the limit, or a failed kernel or read-back. The caller then runs its CPU grid. There is no `unwrap` on a GPU future.
- `camcraft-ui`: `headless_gpu.rs` now re-exports the moved policy. No call site changed.
- `camcraft-motion`: a lib test writes and checks the recorded grid fixture (`crates/gpu/tests/fixtures/facet_grid_2619.grid`). Motion gets no GPU dependency.
- `xtask`: `ALL_CRATES`, `BATCH_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` name `gpu`. The gate tests that count crates and follow the crate reach now include `gpu`. The batch prebuild fixture writes the `gpu` crate.
- The root `Cargo.toml` adds `wgpu = "=30.0.1"`. This is a new direct dependency. It is the same version that `egui-wgpu` 0.36.2 already locks. `Cargo.lock` adds only the `camcraft-gpu` entry, so the lock still has one wgpu.
- The decision entry is `docs/decisions/2620-gpu-compute-seam.md`. It covers the new crate edge `camcraft-ui -> camcraft-gpu`, the wgpu pin, and the dropped options.

The reviewer must set `needs-maintainer`: this PR adds a new direct dependency (`wgpu`).

## Cause

The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They had no GPU access. Only `camcraft-ui` linked wgpu, and the headless device policy was in the UI crate. This PR is slice 2 of #2526. It is part of the fix of #3336 (the stock simulation is slow because it does not use the GPU).

## Tests

- `camcraft-gpu` `bin_parity`:
  - `twin_bins_hold_every_f64_grid_entry`: the CPU twin of the kernel holds each f64 entry of the recorded #2619 grid.
  - `gpu_bins_hold_every_f64_grid_entry_when_an_adapter_exists`: the GPU result holds each f64 entry. Without an adapter, the test prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` makes the skip fail.
  - `twin_and_gpu_bins_hold_the_f64_cells_of_off_border_boxes` (new on this head): 200 boxes with edges inside cells, on a far origin.
- `camcraft-gpu` `refusals`: non-finite boxes and specs, a plan past the device limits, an empty set, no compute, and the off switch. Each gives an `Err` with the reason.
- `camcraft-gpu` unit tests: the probe (WebGL2, a missing compute flag, zero workgroup storage, default limits) and the switch values.
- `camcraft-motion` `gpu_parity_fixture_matches_the_grid`: the recorded fixture matches the f64 grid byte for byte.
- On this machine, the GPU path ran on the hardware adapter "Apple M3 Max" via Metal: 4349 f64 entries, 4921 binned. The earlier head ran the GPU path on the WARP software adapter (Windows).
- Red before the fix: not applicable. This is a new crate, so the tests cannot run on unchanged code. The mutations below show that the pins catch errors.

Mutation results (each mutation was restored after the run):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `binning.wgsl`: inner loop `cx <= x1` changed to `cx < x1` | red: `GPU: facet 0 missing from cell 41` |
| `binning.wgsl`: `cell` gives `floor(v / s) + 1.0` | red: `GPU (off border): facet 68 missing from cell 4` |
| `binning.rs`: `cell32` gives `floor + 1.0` | red: `CPU twin (off border): facet 68 missing from cell 4`. The recorded fixture alone stayed green, so the off-border test was added. |
| `switch.rs`: only `"0"` turns compute off | red: `off_values_turn_compute_off_by_name` |

The f32 margin in `pad_boxes` has no red mutation. A margin error shows only at a cell border with a rounding error, and the fixture coordinates are exact in f32.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-gpu`: green.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: green (274 unit tests and the integration binaries).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `f5ba0a0f8`: 1083 of 1084 steps green, 27.6 min. The root manifest changed, so quick runs the batch plan. The gpu steps (build, lib, `bin_parity`, `refusals`), `ui gpu_render` and clippy were green.
  - The one red step was `app suites: machine` (`a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door`). That test was red on the base `7a626a7f5`, because #3279 made `router` a real kind. #3340 fixed it on main.
  - Then `upstream/main` (`174584111`, which has #3340) was merged into the branch with no conflict. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine` is green after the merge (33 passed).
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans 258 steps (the motion and app heavy lanes). The reach comes only from the `#[cfg(test)]` additions in `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/grid.rs` and `grid_tests.rs`. These lanes were NOT run. The PR must not be flagged ready until they run on the final head.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on macOS in `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`needless_bool`). This PR does not change that file. The lint shows only on non-Windows targets, because a `cfg(windows)` block is compiled out. The gate's clippy step does not include `xtask`.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted output changes in this slice. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The lavapipe (Mesa) software adapter on the Linux runners. The GPU path ran on Metal (macOS) and on WARP (Windows).
- A real device-lost event. The callback code is in `shared.rs`, but no test forces a device loss.
- A wasm32 build of the crate.
- No production caller uses the kernel yet. The wiring into the app is #2621.

## Overlaps

- #3304 (zh-CN i18n draft) changes the root `Cargo.toml` (the workspace member list and the workspace dependencies) and `crates/ui/Cargo.toml` (the dependency list). It adds different lines. Whichever PR merges second refreshes.

Process change: yes

Changelog: The new `camcraft-gpu` crate gives headless GPU compute to the CLI, MCP and tests. It has a capability probe, one cached device, the `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` switch, a CPU fallback with a logged reason, and a facet binning kernel with parity tests.

Refs #3336
Fixes #2620

title: fix(2d): Pass starts at (Auto/Inside/Outside) for 2D Offset
body:
## What changed

A 2D Offset with an Outside containment cut each level core-first. On the band between the stock reach and the part, the core is the middle of the band. So the first ring was a full slot in the stock (#3316).

This PR adds the shared parameter `PassStart { Auto, Inside, Outside }` and gives it to 2D Offset only.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs`: the type and its ring law (`PassStart::rank`).
  - Auto: the core first. This is the old `Reverse(k)` stable sort, byte for byte.
  - Outside: the outer boundary family (counter-clockwise loops) from the boundary in, then the hole family from the core back to its wall. On an Outside band the tool starts outside the stock and ends on the part wall.
  - Inside: the mirror.
- `waterscan.rs`: `waterline_passes` reads the rank. New entry points `pocket_started` and `pocket_avoid_started`. The old entry points and `plan_passes` call them with Auto, so the 3-D pocket, the HSM fallback and rest machining do not change. `plan_passes` moves to `pocket_plan.rs` (400-line law).
- `OpParams::Offset2D.pass_start`: seed Auto. `EditOperationParams` carries it with undo. The digest writes it only off Auto.
- Project key `pass_start` (`PassStartDto`). `auto` is never written. No version step.
- MCP: the generic `edit_operation` patch. The patch guard keeps an explicit `"auto"`. An unknown word is refused. Skill row in `camcraft-mcp`.
- UI: one Passes-tab row `Pass starts at` (`pass_start_row.rs`), shown for 2D Offset.
- User guide row and the decision file `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md` (it leaves room for the #1448 start point).

## Readings

fig8.step, EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, Clearance top of stock +10, Top +0, Bottom selection +1.5, Stepdown 10, hop off, stock box 5 mm past the part:
- Before (Auto): the first ring of each level starts 0.000 mm outside the stock box (in the stock).
- After (Outside): the first ring starts 4.000 mm outside the stock (the ring at the stock edge plus the tool radius). Each level ends 4.000 mm from the part outline, on the wall.
- Auto and Outside: zero lateral rapids below Z 32, and no `RapidInStock` warning.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-app` `offset_pass_start`:
  - `fig8_outside_offset_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` (red on the old order: the first ring was 0.000 mm outside the stock).
  - `fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane` (Auto keeps the old order; #3319 guard).
  - `mcp_sets_pass_start_refuses_an_unknown_word_and_undo_restores_it` (MCP, undo, project round-trip).
- `camcraft-motion` lib `pass_start::tests::auto_is_core_first_and_the_two_sides_mirror`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::pass_start::*` (2 tests) and the 2D Offset row in `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`.

## Quick gate (debug, final head except the clippy allow line and a hint text, which were checked by clippy and the UI lib run)

- motion: lib 533 ok; `machining2d` 68 ok; `corner_arc_radius` 8 ok; `rest2d` 13 ok; `equal_steps` 13 ok.
- app: lib 297 ok; `offset_pass_start` 3 ok; `roughing2d` 7 ok (`offset_kind_is_the_pockets_ring_tiling`); `golden_cl` 33 ok; `conformance` 7 ok; `corner_relief` 4 ok; `corner_relief_safety` 3 ok; `shoulder_adaptive` 7 ok; `do_not_touch` 3 ok; `open_band` 7 ok; `keep_law` 31 ok; `blind_slot` 4 ok; `adaptive_pinch` 1 ok; `tilted_gouge_kinds` 10 ok; `setup_align_2d_kinds` 8 ok; `adaptive_trochoid` 12 ok; `project_roundtrip` 76 ok; `mcp` 23 ok; `mcp_compact` 7 ok; `mcp_enum_patch` 3 ok; `mcp_doc_drift` 6 ok.
- ui: lib 1425 ok.

- The goldens are byte-identical: `golden_cl` and `conformance` pass with no golden change.

## Heavy lanes

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 242 steps (204 app heavy, 37 motion heavy, 1 release build). They were too long for this run. Each one is **not run**:

title: fix(2d): take a picked contour start under control or wear compensation
body:
## What changed

- A closed 2D Contour now takes a user-set start point with Control or Wear compensation. Before, `pick_ring` refused the pick for both modes.
- The ring starts at the projection of the pick, as it does with computer compensation.
- A new module, `contour_comp_pick.rs`, proves the compensation seam law at the pick. `push_span` calls it only for a picked ring. The law has three parts:
  - The first cut after the G41/G42 engage and the last cut before the G40 cancel are straight moves.
  - The two cuts are on one line through the seam. Thus the engage offset and the cancel offset are the same.
  - Under Control only, the programmed part contour is also straight at the seam. Its nearest point is not a part vertex, and its edge is parallel to the first cut.
- A pick that does not obey the law is refused by name. The refusal is `start point (x, y): <mode> compensation needs the seam on a straight run - ...`. The seam does not move to the automatic mid-run seam.
- `SpanCtx` has a new field, `picked`. `contour_comp::closest` is now `pub(super)`.

## Cause

Item 4 of #1473 was not done. The automatic compensated seam is put mid-run by `seam_mid_run`, so it obeys the law by construction. A pick can be on a corner arc or on a vertex. The old `push_span` square check can accept a seam on a chord of an outside corner arc, where the nearest part point is the part vertex. Wear had no seam check at all. So a pick needs its own proof before it is taken.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/motion/tests/contour_start_comp.rs`. All 5 were red on unchanged code ("a picked start is not taken with control compensation yet"):
- `a_picked_start_under_control_compensation_engages_every_level_at_its_projection`
- `a_picked_start_under_wear_compensation_engages_every_level_at_its_projection`
- `a_compensated_pick_on_a_corner_arc_is_refused_by_name_not_moved`
- `a_compensated_pick_on_a_sharp_corner_is_refused_by_name_not_moved`
- `a_compensated_pick_mid_run_in_a_bore_is_taken`

New unit tests in `contour_comp_pick.rs`:
- `a_straight_centre_chord_over_a_part_vertex_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_seam_mid_run_on_a_straight_wall_holds`

Expected change: `control_compensation_with_a_pick_is_refused_by_name` in `crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs` pinned the old refusal of a mid-run pick. That pick is now taken. The test is renamed `control_compensation_with_a_corner_pick_is_refused_by_name` and picks a corner. The `#[test]` count does not go down.

Mutation checks (each guard disabled, then restored):
- The whole `picked_seam` call removed: the corner-arc, sharp-corner and renamed `contour_start` pins go red. With Wear only, the generator posted a corner seam with 2 spans ("expected a refusal, got 22 moves with 2 spans").
- The collinear-cuts guard removed: `a_compensated_pick_on_a_sharp_corner_is_refused_by_name_not_moved` goes red.
- The part-vertex guard removed: `a_straight_centre_chord_over_a_part_vertex_is_refused_by_name` goes red. In the generated paths the arc guard fires first, so this guard is a backstop. The unit test pins it directly.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (145 steps, 0 failed, 26.8 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. Before this change, no path took a pick under compensation.

## Not exercised

- The post output of a picked compensated span. The span is the same `CompSpan` type that the automatic seam makes, so the post code path does not change.
- A picked exit point under compensation. It stays refused by name (the cancel block must leave from the seam of the ring).
- Items 5 to 7 of #1473 (open chains, tilted contours, other operations). They stay open.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `contour_comp.rs`, `contour_start.rs`, `contour.rs` or `crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs`.

Changelog: A closed 2D Contour takes a picked start point with control or wear compensation; a pick where G41/G42 cannot engage and cancel on one straight run is refused by name.

Refs #1473 (item 4 only; items 5 to 7 stay open, so this PR does not close the issue)

title: ci(release): a site_only dispatch can take the app of an earlier run
body:
﻿## What changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: the existing `workflow_dispatch` gets an optional string input `app_run_id` (default empty).
- When `site_only` is true and `app_run_id` is not empty, the `site` job does these steps:
  - It checks that the id has only digits. Any other value stops the job.
  - It downloads the `wasm-app` artifact of that run with `run-id: ${{ inputs.app_run_id }}` and `github-token: ${{ github.token }}`. This step has no `continue-on-error`.
  - It runs `web/check-app-page.sh` on the download, and again on the copy at `app/`. On this path, a failed check is an error.
- The `site` job gets the permission `actions: read`. It gets no other new permission.
- The input goes into scripts only through `env:`. No `run:` script has `${{ inputs.* }}`.
- `docs/decisions/3276-site-app-artifact.md` records the decision and the dropped options.

## Why it is safe

- No new trigger. The input is on the existing `workflow_dispatch`. Only a collaborator can start a dispatch, and a fork PR cannot start it.
- `publish` is unchanged. A `site_only` run never publishes.
- The tag path, a plain dispatch and a `site_only` dispatch without `app_run_id` keep their behaviour. On these paths the new steps are skipped, and `APP_RUN_ID` is empty in `env:`.
- `actions: read` lets the job token read artifacts of this repository only. The job gets no write permission.

title: feat(post): add the G-EDM 2-axis wire EDM post (g-edm.cps)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/g-edm.cps`, registry name "G-EDM Wire EDM". It serves `wire_edm` machines only. "Generic ISO Wire EDM" stays the default (`WIRE_POSTS[0]`).
- The post writes Grbl-family words only: `G21` / `G20 G90 G17`, `G0` to the threading point, `G1`, `G2` / `G3` with incremental `I J`, and `M30`.
- The post writes no `%` fence, no `O` word, no `F`, no `G40` / `G41` / `G42`, and no work offset word.
- The post reads no `edm.codes`. The condition id is a comment. The header says that the operator sets the spark power at the controller.
- The header has `(NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)`.
- The post writes one vertical 2-axis wire section for each program.
- These items are refused by name, and no cut is written for the section:
  - a machine that is not `wire_edm`, a rotary, `edm.awt: true`;
  - `WireTaper` not 0, `WireFourAxis`, `WireU` / `WireV`, `WireAngle`;
  - each `COMP` record (G41 / G42);
  - skims;
  - a work offset other than G54;
  - `SpindleSpeed` above 0, `onToolChange`, `onCycle`, a `Z` change;
  - `AfterOperation` `home`, `stop` and `optional-stop`;
  - a second wire section in the same program.
- Registered in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS`) and `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS`, `embedded()`).
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: `WIRE_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS` name the new post.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, the user guide pages `posting.md` and `machines.md`, and `docs/decisions/2700-g-edm-post.md`.

## Cause

`wire-iso.cps` requires `edm.codes.condition` and `edm.codes.comp_off`, and it writes `%` fences. A G-EDM build sets spark power at the controller and has no condition word. A raw Grbl parser rejects `%`. So no shipped post served a G-EDM build.

## Readings

- #2697 has no new answer from the reporter. The unconfirmed items (`F` and Grbl `error:22`, `G40`, `G54`-`G59`, `M0` pauses, a return move) are not written. The decision file gives the reason for each.
- No `F` word: if G-RBLv3 keeps the Grbl `error:22` check, the controller stops at the first `G1`, before any cut. That is a visible stop, not a wrong cut.
- One section for each program: without a confirmed `M0`, the program cannot stop to cut the wire and thread it again. A `G0` to a second start point would pull the threaded wire through the work.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/g_edm_post.rs` (8 tests):

- `g_edm_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` (golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/wire_slug_punch.nc`, through `posting::post_script`, machine fixture without `edm.codes`)
- `g_edm_post_serves_wire_edms_only_and_is_never_the_default`
- `g_edm_inch_and_arc_words`
- `g_edm_refuses_taper_four_axis_and_lean_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_a_mill_machine_and_a_milling_stream_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told`

Script suite `crates/post/tests/script_g_edm.rs`: 11 recorded streams, each a named refusal (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`).

Red before the fix: all 8 app pins failed with `built-in post G-EDM Wire EDM is not in the registry`.

Mutations (each guard turned off, the pins run, then restored):

- skim guard off: `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name` red
- `onRadiusCompensation` guard off: `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name` red
- one-section guard off: `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told` red
- taper guard off: `g_edm_refuses_taper_four_axis_and_lean_by_name` red
- all restored: 8 of 8 green

Expected change: `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` counts the shipped posts. The count goes from 20 to 21. `g-edm.cps` passes every per-post check of that test.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on head `f3721d6a8`: 758 steps, 0 failed (`gate-logs/quick-20261122-075717`).

None. The new goldens are only under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/` and `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`. No existing golden changed.

## Not exercised

- The output was not run on a G-EDM controller or on G-RBLv3.

title: fix(import): resolve OBJ face references against vertex records
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/obj.rs`: the reader keeps one entry for each `v` record, in file order. Each entry holds the index of its unique position.
- A face reference (positive or negative) resolves against the number of records read so far. Then it maps to the unique position.
- Duplicate positions are still shared. The `MAX_VERTICES` cap on unique positions does not change.
- `resolve_ref` returns `usize`, so a record number does not go through `u32`.

## Cause

The reader merged duplicate positions and did not store the repeated record. Then it resolved face references against the short unique list. A legal file that repeats a vertex record was refused (`vertex reference '5' out of range`). A reference in range of the short list could also name the wrong position.

## Pinning tests

New file `crates/app/tests/obj_vertex_records.rs` (10 tests). Six tests were red on `origin/main` and are green with the fix:

- `obj_positive_indices_after_repeated_records_resolve` (the example of the issue)
- `obj_negative_indices_after_repeated_records_resolve`
- `obj_negative_index_counts_records_seen_so_far`
- `obj_slash_forms_after_repeated_records_resolve`
- `obj_reference_past_the_records_is_refused`
- `obj_face_of_three_repeated_records_is_degenerate` (main said "out of range"; now "degenerate triangle")

Four refusal tests were green before and after: `obj_forward_reference_is_refused`, `obj_zero_reference_is_refused`, `obj_negative_reference_past_the_start_is_refused`, `obj_huge_and_garbage_references_are_refused`.

## Gates (head of this PR)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 32 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also run: the `import`, `import_bytes`, `winding_align` and `cadmpeg_import` binaries: all pass.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` lists 205 steps ("app heavy: every target", because `obj.rs` is in `crates/app`). I ran the import-related steps by `--only`:
  - `kernel heavy: step_agreement`: ok
  - `app heavy: continuous_4axis_part` (imports an `.obj` example model): ok
  - `app heavy: large_models`: ok

The other 202 heavy steps did not run. They do not read OBJ files through this change, but "not run" is not a pass. The reviewer or the cut gate runs them.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3298-obj-vertex-records.md`.

Changelog: OBJ import accepts faces that refer to repeated vertex records, with positive and negative indices (#3298).

title: feat(cl): translate, XY turn, A/B turn and vertical mirror for toolpaths
body:
## What changed

- A new module `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` with three sub-files (`transform_rotary.rs`, `transform_mirror.rs`, `transform_climb.rs`). `camcraft-app` re-exports it as `app::cl::transform`.
- `translate(tp, [dx, dy, dz])` shifts every move, arc center, canned cycle, compensated span and edge break.
- `transform_xy(tp, tx, ty, angle_deg, pivot)` turns the path in XY about a pivot and then shifts it. Nesting (#2166) can call it directly.
- `rotate_about_axis(tp, RotaryAxis::A | B, origin, angle_deg, chord_tol)` turns the path about X or Y. Each move states the turned tool axis. Arcs become chords at `chord_tol`.
- `mirror_plane(tp, MirrorPlane, MirrorMode)` mirrors the path across a vertical plane.
  - `GeometricMirror` gives the exact mirror image: G2 <-> G3 and G41 <-> G42.
  - `PreserveClimb(PassFamily)` mirrors and then runs each pass backwards between its entry and its retract. The lead-out becomes the lead-in. The arcs keep their original G2/G3, and the compensated spans keep their original side.
- `TransformError` names each refusal: `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, `RotaryMove`, `TiltedMove`, `PlasmaCut`, `VerticalArc`, `CannedCycleTilt`, `HorizontalMirrorPlane`, `TiltedMirrorPlane`, `BadInput`, `NotReversible(why)`.
- The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3011-cl-transforms.md`.

## Cause

This is new work. The codebase had no shared transform for toolpaths. Patterns, mirror folders and nesting need one.

## Design

- All four transforms use one map, `p -> M p + t`, with `M` orthogonal.
- An arc keeps its plane only when `M` maps the plane normal exactly onto plus or minus itself. Its turn direction flips when `det(M)` times that sign is negative. This one rule gives the G2/G3 swap under a mirror. It also finds the XZ / YZ arcs that a transform cannot keep.
- Moves, arc centers and cycles snap to the 1 um lattice. Edge-break polylines do not snap, because a snap would move framed caps off orthonormal.
- `PreserveClimb` accepts only contour, profile and chamfer paths. It refuses these by name:
  - a helical ramp, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing and other families;
  - a ramp or helical entry;
  - a level change without a retract;
  - a cut before the first pass or after the last pass;
  - a link that is not on the clearance plane.

## Tests (pins)

All 20 tests are in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_tests.rs` and `transform_mirror_tests.rs` (`cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`):

- `translate_shifts_every_record_to_the_micron`, `translate_refuses_a_non_finite_offset`
- `transform_xy_turns_a_quarter_about_the_pivot_then_shifts`, `transform_xy_at_thirty_degrees_is_micron_accurate`, `transform_xy_refuses_a_vertical_arc_it_cannot_keep`
- `rotate_about_a_turns_the_point_and_states_the_axis`, `rotate_about_b_flattens_arcs_within_the_chord_tolerance`, `rotate_about_an_axis_by_zero_is_the_identity`, `rotate_about_an_axis_refuses_a_tilted_canned_cycle`
- `every_transform_refuses_thread_cycles_probe_touches_and_c_moves`
- `geometric_mirror_swaps_g2_g3_and_g41_g42`, `geometric_mirror_on_a_diagonal_plane_is_micron_accurate`, `mirror_refuses_horizontal_and_tilted_planes`, `mirror_refuses_tilted_moves`
- `preserve_climb_reverses_the_pass_between_entry_and_retract`, `preserve_climb_reverses_two_depths_linked_on_the_clearance_plane`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_helical_entry`, `preserve_climb_refuses_clearing_families_by_name`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_cut_before_the_first_pass`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_level_change_without_a_retract`

Before the fix, the pins did not compile (`translate`, `mirror_plane`, `TransformError` ... did not exist).

Mutation checks: I removed each guard, ran the pins (all red), and restored the guard (green):

- the G2/G3 flip: 3 pins red
- the G41/G42 swap: 2 pins red
- the side restore in the climb reversal: 1 pin red
- the probe refusal: 1 pin red
- the refusal of a cut before the first pass: 1 pin red
- the horizontal-plane refusal: 1 pin red
- the pass reversal: 2 pins red
- the tilted-cycle refusal: 1 pin red

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on a273ee018: 1077 steps, 0 failed, clippy included. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No existing code calls the module yet.

## Not exercised

- No caller exists yet: patterns, mirror folders and nesting (#2166) will use it.
- No posted G-code goes through a transformed path in this PR.
- The framed edge-break caps under a turn and under a mirror are not pinned by a test.

## Overlaps

#3046 adds a line to the module list of `crates/cl/src/cl/mod.rs` (the same file, but a different line). The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: CL toolpath transforms: translate, XY turn, A/B axis turn and vertical-plane mirror (G2/G3 and G41/G42 swap, or a climb-preserving pass reversal), with named refusals.

Fixes #3011

title: feat(post): Fanuc option to write the stock as a Manual Guide i blank (G1902 / G1900)
body:
## What changed

- The Fanuc post (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps`) has a new option, "Manual Guide i blank (G1902 / G1900)" (`manualGuideBlank`). The default is off.
- With the option on, the post writes one blank block for each program. The block comes after `G21` / `G20` and before the first `G90 G54` and `T.. M6`.
  - A box stock gives `G1902 B D H I J K`. Example: a 100 x 60 x 30 block with G54 at the top centre gives `G1902 B100. D60. H30. I50. J30. K30.`
  - A round bar along Z with its axis on the work origin gives `G1900 D L K`. K is `StockZTop - OriginZ`, the distance from the work origin to the positive-Z end face (Fanuc B-63874EN/05, printed page 193, PDF page 215). A diameter 60, length 30 bar with a top-face origin gives `G1900 D60. L30. K0.`. An origin below the top face gives positive K. A negative K produces a refusal comment instead of a blank block.
  - Each other stock gives the comment `(NO BLANK BLOCK - <reason>)` and no block.
- The app stream has three new PARAMs after `StockZTop`: `StockShape`, `StockShapeBottom` and `StockShapeDiameter` (a bar only). A new module writes them: `crates/app/src/posting_stock_shape.rs`. `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` has the new row.
- The Heidenhain Klartext post refuses each PARAM that is not on its positive list. It now ignores the three new PARAMs. Its output does not change. Without this change, `klartext_builtin` failed with "unsupported parameter StockShape".
- A tester kit for the Robodrill is in `docs/tester-kits/fanuc-mgi-blank/`. A test pins it to the post output, byte for byte.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/2769-mgi-blank.md`.

## Cause

This is a new feature. The research comment on #2769 gives the addresses. The stream did not tell a box from a bar or from a model stock. The stream also did not state the stock bottom for a mill without a controller identity.

- Red before the fix:
  - With the upstream `fanuc.cps`, 8 of the first 9 post pins fail. Only the off-by-default pin passes, as it must.

- Mutations (each one red, then green after the restore):
  - Restored the old lower-end K expression: `a_z_bar_on_the_origin_posts_g1900`, `a_z_bar_with_the_origin_below_its_top_posts_the_end_face_distance`, and `the_tester_kit_is_what_the_post_writes` fail (9 passed, 3 failed). Restore: 12 passed.

title: feat(i18n): multi-language registry, zh-CN catalogue, CJK font and picker (draft)
body:
## What

A reviewable pilot for #853: a **data-driven language registry**, a Simplified
Chinese catalogue (English as source and fallback), a bundled CJK font, and a
live language picker. Doubles as an architecture proposal for the issue's open
questions. Opened as a **draft** because #853 is currently `P?` (paused) —
please set a priority / pick a mechanism before treating this as ready.

## Scope

### One registry, not a hardcoded pair

`Lang` is a descriptor; every shipped language is one row of `REGISTRY` in
`crates/i18n`. `Lang::ALL`, locale parsing, the parse-once catalogue cache and
the View door's picker all derive from that row — adding a language is a
catalogue file plus a row, with no change to lookup logic or any call site. A
test names any inconsistent row (duplicate tag, missing native name, tag that
does not round-trip, unreadable catalogue).

### Coverage

`assets/i18n/zh-CN.toml` now ships **3,638 strings**. The surface covered by
this branch includes:

- ribbon commands, groups and section captions; tree section headers and
  literal rows (user names are never translated); machine and operation tabs
- shared property vocabulary, operation headers, help/hover text, consequence
  lines, action-bar hover/disabled reasons, status banner lines
- static literals at direct egui call sites (`on_hover_text`, `label`, `button`,
  `checkbox`, `menu_item`, `Label/RichText/Button::new`) — 653+ call sites
- 106 frequently used UI string constants
- **dynamic `format!` templates** through `tf()`: the template is the catalogue
  key, so Chinese can reorder words; arguments are pre-rendered and substituted
  in the translated template's placeholder order. 1,553 unique templates in
  `crates/app` and 766 in `crates/ui` are routed, with **0 missing keys**
- **status line, refusal and page-label templates** in `crates/ui` (72 call
  sites across 32 files), including the timed import/refresh line where the
  verb is translated at its own seam

Coverage is enforced structurally: scripts extract static strings reaching
`tr()` and dynamic templates reaching `tf()`, and confirm 0 missing keys.

### Font

`assets/ui/fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular-Subset.ttf` is Noto Sans SC 400 subset to
GB2312 + punctuation (8,090 code points, 2.3 MB, OFL 1.1), embedded with
`include_bytes!`. A test reads the TTF's `cmap` directly to prove every shipped
string is covered.

### Language choice

Follows the system locale (`LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG`); `CAMCRAFT_LANG`
overrides for one run; the View door's **Language** list switches live and
persists to `prefs.json`. The list is generated from `Lang::ALL`, so a new
registry row appears there without a UI change.

## Deliberately not translated

Nothing that must never be localised is routed through the catalogue:
G-code, CL, project files, `.mch`/`.cps`, MCP tool names and JSON, parsed log
lines and test goldens. English is the key, so a miss shows English — never a
key or a blank. Also left alone: wordless concatenation templates (`{n}`,
dimension-only rows) and format names/paths. Refusal **codes** matched by
`starts_with()` stay in English as stable identity, while their displayed
sentences are translated and the match accepts either form — a regression
test proves a translated refusal still retires in every language.

## Integration note

Rebased onto current `main`. The upstream refactor moved the operation header
into `egui_app/op_page/header.rs`; commit `57468bfa` re-applies the translations
there. `08c8c91f` adds `Undercut` / `V-Carve`. `e2ab79fe` expands static
coverage; `19eed997` adds `tf()` and translates the dynamic UI layer;
`89172375` / `b818cf79` translate app-layer messages and labels drawn outside
`tr()` helpers. One head adds the data-driven registry and the status/label seam; the
latest adds translated refusal heads (commit `0093244c`) with a stable-code
match that survives a language switch.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-i18n -p camcraft-app --all-targets` — passes, no warnings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-i18n` — 12 passed + 1 doctest (incl. the new registry-law test)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib i18n_tests` — 4 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib fonts::tests` — 4 passed (glyph coverage of every shipped string)
- `python3 scripts/i18n/check.py assets/i18n/zh-CN.toml` — 3,638 strings, 0 errors
- static + dynamic coverage scans: 0 strings reaching `tr()`/`tf()` without a Chinese entry in `crates/ui` and `crates/app`

## Design docs

`docs/I18N.md` and `docs/decisions/853-ui-translations.md` record the
architecture, the registry law, the measurements and the deliberate scope
boundary.

title: fix(xtask): name the signal or crash status of a test executable that dies
body:
## What changed

The gate now writes the reason when a direct test executable stops without an exit code. A signal can kill the process, or the process can stop on a crash status. Before this change, the step log and the step note showed only `exit -1`.

- New module `xtask/src/exit_status.rs`. On Unix it names the signal and the core dump (`killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV), core dumped`). On Windows it names the known crash statuses (`status 0xC0000005 (access violation)`).
- `direct::run` writes a line `gate: the test executable stopped: <how>` into the step log.
- `exec::read_log` puts the reason into the step note: `FAIL 1s ui suites: trace_parity exit -1 (killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV))`.

The PR adds no host lock. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3258-gate-names-the-crash.md`.

## Root cause of #3258 (evidence)

The repository has no shared resource that two runs on one host use at the same time. The cause was a hardware Vulkan driver on the runner hosts. That cause is outside the repository, and the runner environment fixed it.

- Each red UI step stopped in the middle of its tests, with no panic. I compared each log with a green log of the same binary. The tests that did not finish are the GPU tests:
  - trace_parity (egg, 44950073227): `the_gpu_sees_the_box_the_cpu_sees` and `deviation_classes_agree_with_the_cpu_verdict`.
  - egui_app (wopr, 44955923206): `a_headless_start_with_a_model_file_imports_and_draws_it`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` and `a_headless_start_with_a_project_file_opens_and_draws_it`.
- `exit -1` is the gate's value for "no exit code": a signal killed the process (`st.code().unwrap_or(-1)` in `direct::run`).
- mkinney's kernel logs show a segfault in `libvulkan.so` on skull and egg at the failure times. The runners pinned Mesa's software Vulkan at about 22:40 UTC. All three UI failures came before that time.
- mkinney found no kernel segfault and no OOM on wopr. The wopr abort is attributed to the driver only by its time (before the 22:40 UTC pin), not by a log line.
- About 30 post-merge runs came after the pin, and many of them ran at the same time. None of them has a UI `exit -1`. The red runs between 02:41 and 04:10 are deterministic test failures (`slot_dxf_sketch`, `example_catalog`), not this signature.
- The uma failure (44987903117, `bore_core`) has a different cause. It was `PermissionDenied` on a PID-named directory in a shared `/tmp`, and #3290 fixed it.

The two runner-level stops with no log are not covered: the skull run that hung (44982953354) and the uma run that lost communication with the server (44995766211, attempt 1). Follow-up #3303 tracks them.

## Tests

- The pin reserves its temp directory with an atomic `create_dir` and steps past `AlreadyExists`, as `fixture_dir` in `crates/app/tests/bore_core.rs` does (#3290).
- Pin: `exit_status::tests::a_crashed_step_executable_says_how_it_stopped_in_its_log_and_note`. It runs a crashing child through `direct::run`: `sh -c 'kill -SEGV $$'` on Unix, and `cmd /c exit -1073741819` on Windows. I removed the `direct.rs` change, and the pin failed (`no stop line in: Running crash (cmd)`). With the fix, the pin passes.
- `a_signal_death_names_the_signal_and_the_core_dump` (Unix), `a_crash_status_names_the_crash` (Windows), `a_plain_exit_code_has_no_crash_words`, `the_note_carries_how_the_executable_stopped`.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green on Windows.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on 8f1f47035 (xtask unit tests, 183 s, 0 failed).

## Not exercised

- I ran the tests on Windows only. The Unix test and the Unix branch of the pin will run on the post-merge runner.
- The historical abort was not reproduced. The new line shows its signal on the next occurrence.

Changelog: none (gate tooling: a step that a signal kills now names the signal in its log and note)

Process change: yes

Effort: medium

Fixes #3258

title: feat(post): add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (.mmg format)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/richauto.cps` for the RichAuto DSP A11 router controller.
- The post is registered as `"RichAuto DSP A11"` in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`). It comes after Mach4, at the end of the mill posts.
- The output follows the `.mmg` program that a Laguna Swift A11 runs (#1907, comment of 2026-11-18). The comment of 2026-11-18 on this issue names that program as the conformance target.
  - The file extension is `.mmg`.
  - Each block has a sequence number: `N10`, then steps of 10. Comment lines and the `%` line have no number.
  - There are no spaces between words.
  - Lengths have three decimals. `F` is mm/min with one decimal.
  - Rapid is `G00` and feed is `G1`. The spindle starts with `M03S<rpm>` and stops with `M05`.
  - An axis word or an `F` word that does not change is not written.
  - The program ends with `M30` and then a `%` line.
- The setup block is `G21G90G17`. The post writes no `G54`, `G40`, `G80`, `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, `G49`, `T` or `M6` word.
- Offset 1 is the work origin that the operator sets on the pendant. Offsets 2 and higher are refused by name.
- Arcs use incremental `I`/`J`/`K` (`AbsCntr = Off`). An arc of more than 180 degrees is split.
- Drilling cycles are expanded to plain `G00`/`G1` moves, with the floor dwell and the bore spindle stop and restart.
- The `SpindleDwellMs` option writes `G04P<ms>` after the spindle start. The default is 0.
- The post refuses these by name: tapping, `G41`/`G42`, probing, rotary moves, `G96`, a second tool, an inch document, a bad rpm, a bad coolant, and a missing or low clearance plane.
- The post writes header notes (#2996) and WARN records as `(...)` comments.

## Cause

The shipped posts do not run safely on an A11. They write `G91.1`, `G53`, `T.. M6`, `G43` and canned cycles. A basic A11 firmware can refuse these words.

## Tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_richauto.rs` and `crates/post/tests/richauto_safety/mod.rs`: 41 tests, including the 11 recorded-stream goldens of `post_suite!`.
- The pin `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format` was red on the older held script (format without `N`, `%`): `the program ends with %`. It is green on the new script.
- On `upstream/main` all the pins are red, because the post does not exist.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: RichAuto is added to `POSTS`, `REFUSED` (`tap_plate`, "tapping"), the synth stream (G54, no tap) and `EXTENSIONS` (`mmg`). All 7 tests pass.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`: the count of shipped posts goes from 20 to 21.
- Mutations. Each mutant was run against the pins, then the script was restored and the pins were green again:
  - no final `%` line: 8 tests red, including `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format`;
  - spaces between words: 18 tests red;
  - no modal word omission: 11 tests red, including `unchanged_axis_and_feed_words_are_left_out`;
  - no `onComment` hook: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` red;
  - no sequence step (all blocks `N0`): 7 tests red.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, base `dfbe0d8a5`): 752 of 753 steps pass. The one red step is `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`. It fails in the same way on unchanged `upstream/main` (stale golden `slot_dxf_outline.cl`). I filed it as #3293.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run.

## Goldens moved

- No existing golden changed.
- New: 12 conformance goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/richauto/`, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_richauto.nc`, and 11 recorded goldens in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/richauto/` (6 programs, 5 refusals). I read each one. The arc centres are correct with a non-zero origin.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on an A11 or on the friend's Laguna Swift.
- The A11 response to `G21G90G17`, to `G2`/`G3` with incremental centres and to `G04P` is not confirmed. The sample program has no setup block, no arcs and no dwell.
- The sample program has CRLF line ends. This post writes LF.
- `axisInversion` is not declared. The engine refuses a machine with an inverted axis by name. Grbl 1.1 is the same.

## Overlaps

These open PRs add rows to the same lists (`BUILTINS`, or the lists in `conformance.rs`). They touch other posts and do not change the same function: #3160, #3058, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978, #2974, #2972, #2969, #2968, #2964, #2955, #2951, #2646, #2515. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: New built-in post "RichAuto DSP A11" for RichAuto A11 routers (Laguna Swift, Grizzly): .mmg files with N numbers, one tool, drilling as plain moves, named refusals for tapping, cutter compensation and probing.

Fixes #1914
