title: fix(slot): regenerate the DXF-outline slot golden for the #2906 wall lap
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/tests/golden/slot_dxf_outline.cl` is regenerated.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_dxf_sketch.rs`: `a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` gets two new asserts.
- `docs/decisions/3278-slot-dxf-golden.md` records the decision.

No generator code changes.

## Cause

The post-merge gate is red on `a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` from 6cd4f3e01 (the merge of #3136) on.

- Run 44977365067 on 5bc0b7129 (#3158): green.
- Run 44977387120 on 6cd4f3e01 (#3136): red on this one test.
- Runs on 60c0f48bf, 24da8ad7e and bf7e68b14: red on this one test only.

The branch of #3136 did not contain #2920. Thus #3136 regenerated `slot_wide_channel_rows` but not `slot_dxf_outline.cl`.

The assert was the golden compare, `crates/app/tests/common/mod.rs:253`: `golden ...slot_dxf_outline.cl is stale; regenerate with WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test`. The asserts before it passed on main: the ends (45, 25) and (75, 25), the width 10 mm, and the cut box 42..78 x 22..28.

## Readings: the golden diff

The slot has R 5 ends and the tool is 4 mm, so the cutter centre is h = 3 mm off the axis.

- The header changes from `HSMW-CL v1 ... moves=9` to `HSMW-CL v2 ... moves=15`. The v2 header comes from the arc moves.
- The 9 old moves do not change: the approach, the plunge, and the three rows at d = -3, 0 and 3 with their joins.
- 6 moves are added after the last row, at (75, 28). They are the #2906 wall lap:
  - `Feed` to (45, 28): the +n side.
  - `Arc` to (42, 25) and `Arc` to (45, 22), CCW about (45, 25): the round end at a.
  - `Feed` to (75, 22): the -n side.
  - `Arc` to (78, 25) and `Arc` to (75, 28), CCW about (75, 25): the round end at b.
- Each lap point is 3.000 mm from its arc centre, or 3.000 mm off the axis on a side. The lap cuts the wall to size and stays in the outline.
- The old golden pinned rows that touch each round end only at their end points, with chord joins across the end. That left up to h (1 - cos 45 deg) = 0.88 mm of material on each end. The old shape was the wrong one.

`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test slot_dxf_sketch -- --exact a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` wrote the golden: the test's own path, with no hand edit. A run without `WRITE_GOLDEN` then passed against it.

`trochoid_slot_dxf_outline.cl` does not change: `git diff origin/main` on it is empty, and `a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline` passes.

## Pinning tests

`a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` has two new asserts:

- Each round end has an arc move about its arc centre, with both end points on the 3 mm cutter-centre circle.
- No cutting move leaves the outline at the tool radius. Each end point of each cutting move is at most 3 mm (+1 um) off the axis (45, 25) -> (75, 25). Each arc turns about an axis end, at a radius of at most 3 mm. The cutter-centre stadium is convex, so a line between two points in it stays in it.

The stock-simulation assert `gouge_cells == 0` was hidden behind the stale golden. It now runs again and passes.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate test a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size --crate camcraft-app --binary slot_dxf_sketch --exact` on origin/main 5c8340b81: FAIL. This reproduced the stale golden.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on 4c11e92b7 without the outline-containment assert: 690 steps, 0 failed, 68 min. The diff touches a `.cl` golden, so the plan maps it to all cl, post and app suites. This includes the #3136 pins in `operations`, `clearance_in_stock` and `example_catalog`.
- On the final head (test-only and docs changes after the quick gate): `camcraft-app` `slot_dxf_sketch` 4/4, `slot_caps` 4/4, `slot_extension` 5/5, `slot_picks` 8/8 and `slot_pick_refusals` 3/3. `camcraft-motion` `slot_round_ends` 3/3 (#3136) and `machining2d` 68/68.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test slot_dxf_sketch -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run`: 205 steps. The `.cl` golden maps to every app heavy lane. The count is more than 60, so the heavy lanes were not run. The diff changes no generator code, and `slot_dxf_sketch` has no ignored tests.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (see above).
- The quick gate was not run a second time on the final head. The only later changes are the containment assert in `slot_dxf_sketch.rs` and the decision file. The touched binary ran on the final head.

Changelog: none (test golden only; the behaviour shipped with #3136)

Effort: high

Fixes #3278

title: fix(post): block cutting tools at reserved numbers and names
body:
Stacked on #3157 (merge #3157 first)

## What changed

Machine files accept `tooling.reserved` entries.
Each entry reserves a number, a name, or both for `probe` or `tool_setter`.
The reader and validator refuse malformed entries by key.
Stored projects retain the reservations.

New cutting tools skip reserved numbers.
A probe takes a declared probe pocket.
Tool edits and library imports refuse incompatible reserved numbers or names.
Verification and posting also refuse old unsafe assignments.
The existing GUI, script, and MCP commands use these checks.
Tool number zero remains refused.

The standalone post CLI checks its input before it creates or replaces output.
It retains the loaded tool across sections.
A new TOOL needs its own declared kind.
A stream with no tool selector cannot post motion on a machine with reservations.
Indexed lookups keep the checks bounded for long streams.

The 18 shipped Tormach mill and router files reserve T99 for the probe.
A machine that omits the field reserves nothing.

## Cause

Tool allocation considered only document numbers.
Machine files could not protect a probe pocket or a control-managed tool name.
The app and standalone post paths had no reservation check.

## Before and after screenshots

These captures are reused from parent #3157.
Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted.
The camera looks from the front, and the work envelope is shown.

The after capture has the switch on and shows the viewport marker.

title: feat(multiaxis): Multi-Axis Deburr - tilted chamfer-mill edge breaks with holder tilt-away
body:
## What changed

- A new operation kind, **Multi-Axis Deburr** (`OpType::MultiAxisDeburr`), is appended at ordinal 46 in `Section::MultiAxis`. Stored kind ids do not move.
- It has every field of the 3D Deburr and five more: `axis_mode` (`Axis5` / `Axis4`), `lead_deg`, `lag_deg`, `max_tilt_deg` and `shank_avoid`.
- New kernel `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::multiaxis_deburr` (`deburr_axis.rs`, `deburr_pose.rs`):
  - The tool lays one cone flank on the chamfer plane of each break. The cut is the flat chamfer for every pose that turns the axis about the plane normal.
  - `Axis5` leans the axis inside `max_tilt_deg`. `Axis4` keeps the axis square to the A axis (about X).
  - Mandatory continuous facet checks cover the full cone and the supplied physical shank and holder. They cover each complete cut, entry and exit. The stored `shank_avoid` option cannot disable this guard.
  - An edge with no clear pose follows the Deburr's unreachable-edge policy: skip with a note, or refuse by name.
  - The tool enters and leaves along a checked, bounded axis line. The entire cone stays above `bottom_z`. Pose changes, gaps and chamfer-plane corners split runs.
  - Each run declares a framed flat `EdgeBreak` cap (#1891).
- The exposed-edge scan moved from `finishing3d/deburr.rs` into the shared `finishing3d/deburr_scan.rs`. The 3D Deburr calls it in the same order.
- App wiring: kind row, seed, sanity door (lead minus lag inside the cap), generate arm, cache stamp, project DTO (`multi_axis_deburr`), heights, setup sheet, section mode, WCS refusals, sim break bound.
- MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` work with the new kind through the generic tools.
- UI: `multiaxis_deburr_page.rs` (Geometry: size, filters, unreachable policy; Passes: axis mode, lean, max tilt, shank avoid; Heights; Feeds). The kind has its own original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-multiaxis-deburr.svg`, PNG from `cargo xtask icons`).

## Cause

New feature (#1894). A vertical cone cannot break steep or vertical edges, so the 3D Deburr skips them.

## UI screenshots

The before images show revision `971c23faa026865be47e425a660439f8c3d17ecd`, an ancestor of this PR's base. The new kind is absent there.
The after images show the original feature head `c2560be2bc4f8900f5cc238bb5879742ff8169d5`. The safety fixes below do not change the UI.
These are actual application window captures. They show the operation controls and entry. They do not show generated toolpaths.
The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775`.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Existing 3-axis Deburr page | New Multi-Axis Deburr Geometry page |
| ![Before: 3-axis Deburr page at 971c23fa](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/before-deburr-page-971c23fa.png) | ![After: Multi-Axis Deburr Geometry page at c2560be2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/after-geometry-c2560be2.png) |
| Multi menu without the new entry | Multi menu with the new entry and glyph |
| ![Before: Multi menu at 971c23fa](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/before-multiaxis-entry-971c23fa.png) | ![After: Multi-Axis Deburr entry at c2560be2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/after-multiaxis-entry-c2560be2.png) |

The new Passes page shows the axis mode, lead, lag, tilt cap and shank avoidance controls.

![After: Multi-Axis Deburr Passes page at c2560be2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/after-passes-c2560be2.png)

## Safety review fixes on the new head

Final head: `a312b20ebdb48c2505ec417c6008d5cc1c6569d4`.

- Each candidate trims the edge until the tip and the lowest cone-rim point stay at or above `bottom_z` on every pass.
- Continuous outer convex polyhedra enclose the cone and the physical tool bands along the entire cutting segment.
- Facet clipping permits cone and cutting-flute contact only within the finite requested chamfer prism. Floors, other faces and material past an edge end receive no exemption.
- The same continuous checks cover the complete entry and exit lines. Clearance endpoints must put the whole tool above the part. The first plunge stages the axis change above every part face plus the largest tool radius and 1 mm.
- An axis that is too flat or requires more than 100 tool diameters of reach is refused. Unsafe segments use the existing named skip or refuse policy.
- The app supplies the physical shank and holder even when `shank_avoid` is false. The kernel guards the operation because column stock simulation does not judge posed cuts.

Regression pins:

- `the_brick_keeps_the_tilted_tip_and_entire_cone_above_the_bottom`: complete cone and tip stay above the brick's programmed bottom; clear vertical edges still cut.
- `a_raised_bottom_clips_the_cone_without_a_part_floor_to_hide_the_error`: a raised window isolates the bottom guard from the part floor.
- `a_boss_on_a_floor_skips_the_unsafe_foot_and_still_cuts_the_clear_edge`: the window extends below the floor; the unsafe foot is skipped and the clear upper edge still cuts.
- `an_obstacle_on_the_entry_line_is_skipped_while_clear_edges_still_cut`: an obstacle away from the cut blocks the entry or exit; other edges still cut.
- `an_unsafe_entry_refuses_by_name_when_skipping_is_disabled`: the picked edge cuts without the obstacle and refuses with the obstacle.
- `disabling_shank_avoid_cannot_bypass_the_mandatory_holder_collision_guard`: the option is off; an obstacle that misses the cone and shank still blocks the holder.

Mutation checks (each restored byte for byte):

- Ignored the pose offset in bottom clipping: the raised-window pin failed with a cone below `bottom_z`. Restored: passed.
- Disabled cone facet checks: the boss-floor pin failed with a cone in the floor. Restored: passed.
- Checked only the cut and omitted the entry/exit sweeps: the entry-obstacle pin failed when the tip crossed the obstacle. Restored: passed.
- Omitted the physical shank and holder from the app adapter: the option-off holder pin failed. Restored: passed.
- Sent the first plunge directly to the tip: the existing MCP generation pin failed with two mid-turn shank findings. Restored: passed.

Validation:

- Full quick gate on predecessor `93e571af99028af87a1dbdcf00cae796d57fa628`: 515 of 516 steps passed in 36.5 minutes. Only `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` failed at its existing stale golden. The Slot test and golden are unchanged by this fix.
- The final commit removes one redundant `let` binding. It does not change the guarded geometry or the tests.
- Final-head quick selection: `motion suites: lib` and `app suites: mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed both steps in 1.9 minutes. Motion: 530 passed, 10 ignored. MCP: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the exact final source tree.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 242 steps on the final head in 40.9 minutes. The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six registered known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
- All 13 `multiaxis::deburr_axis_tests` passed in release mode on the final head. This includes all five new kernel safety pins.

The recorded gate runs used `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`. An earlier run with incompatible build artifacts was excluded. No golden, screenshot, log or review image is part of these fix commits.

The earlier checks below apply only to their stated original head. They do not replace the final validation above.

## Earlier evidence follow-up (original head)

Original feature head: `c2560be2bc4f8900f5cc238bb5879742ff8169d5`. This earlier evidence run did not change its source tree.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 242 steps in 33.3 minutes. The run used release mode and `--ignored`. The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`.

title: feat(post): Fanuc AI contour control option (G05.1 Q1 R / Q0)
body:
## What changed

The built-in Fanuc post (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps`) has two new options in the "Smoothing" group:

- `aiContourControl` (boolean, default off): AI contour control (G05.1).
- `aiContourLevel` (integer 1-10, default 5): the R word of `G05.1 Q1`.

With the option on, each operation writes `G05.1 Q1 R<level>` as the last preamble block. That is after `T M6`, `G43 H`, `S M3`, the coolant word and any `G68`. Each operation writes `G05.1 Q0` at its end. That is after `G80`, before `G69`, `M9` and `M5`.

Guards:

- A canned cycle writes `G05.1 Q0` before its cycle block. The Doosan DNM manual cited in `doosan-dnm.cps` requires Q0 before G73-G89.
- A section with the spindle stopped (a touch probe with `G31`) does not arm AICC.
- A level outside 1-10 is refused by name one time, and no `G05.1` is written. The host also refuses it from the declared range.
- With the option on, the #616 note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN" is not written, because the post now writes the control's smoothing words.

With the option off (the default), the output does not change.

## Cause

The machine owner (FANUC Robodrill, 31i-A5) uses AICC on each operation: "G05.1 Q1 R5 in the start of op and then G05.1 Q0 at the end". Before this change, the Fanuc post wrote only a comment for a Smoothing ask (#616), and it had no option for G05.1.

## Tests

New file `crates/post/tests/fanuc_aicc.rs` (7 tests):

- `fanuc_aicc_is_off_by_default`
- `fanuc_aicc_on_brackets_each_operation`
- `fanuc_aicc_level_is_the_option`
- `fanuc_aicc_skips_a_probe_section`
- `fanuc_aicc_level_out_of_range_is_refused_by_name`
- `fanuc_aicc_on_replaces_the_smoothing_not_written_note`
- `fanuc_aicc_options_are_declared_off_and_bounded`

On unchanged `fanuc.cps` (upstream/main), 5 of the 7 tests fail. The two tests that pass check that nothing is written (off by default, probe section).

Mutation results (each mutation fails its pin; restored, all 7 pass):

- Remove `aiccOff()` before the canned cycle: `fanuc_aicc_on_brackets_each_operation` fails.
- Remove the spindle and probe guard in `aiccOn()`: `fanuc_aicc_skips_a_probe_section` fails.
- Remove the level range check: `fanuc_aicc_level_out_of_range_is_refused_by_name` fails.
- Remove the early return in `smoothOn()`: `fanuc_aicc_on_replaces_the_smoothing_not_written_note` fails.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. The option is off by default.

## Not exercised

- No program with the option on was run on a real control. The owner gave the block form. The placement before the first move and the Q0 before canned cycles are not confirmed on the 31i-A5.
- Questions 1 and 2 of the issue (M29 before G84, G73 or G83, the R plane) are still open. The owner has not answered them. This PR does not change them.
- The UI shows the new options through the generic declared-options page. No UI test was added.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2603-fanuc-aicc.md`.

Changelog: Fanuc post: new off-by-default option "AI contour control (G05.1)" writes `G05.1 Q1 R<level>` at each operation start and `G05.1 Q0` at its end (level 1-10, default 5).

Refs #2603

title: ci(release): site_only dispatch builds and deploys only the site
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: the existing `workflow_dispatch` gets a boolean input `site_only` (default `false`).
  - `linux`, `macos`, `windows` and `wasm` have `if: ${{ !inputs.site_only }}`. `aur`, `snap` and `flatpak` need `linux`, so they are skipped too.
  - `publish` stays tag-only. Its condition also has `!inputs.site_only`, so a `site_only` run never publishes.
  - `site` is not changed. It builds from the dispatched ref and reads the version from that tree's `Cargo.toml` (0.25.0 on `site/v0.25.0`). With `wasm` skipped, app/ is the "not part of this copy" page, as for a failed wasm build.
  - `pages` deploys on the tag path as before. It also deploys on a `site_only` dispatch, but only from a `site/*` branch.
- `xtask/tests/release_site_tests.rs`: the new test `site_only_dispatch_runs_only_site_and_pages` pins the triggers, the input and each job condition, `publish` included.
- `docs/decisions/3276-site-redeploy.md`: the decision, the dropped options and the owner action.

## Why it is safe

- No new trigger. The triggers are still the `vX.Y.0` tag push and `workflow_dispatch` (the test pins the list).
- No fork path. Only a collaborator can dispatch a workflow. All jobs are GitHub-hosted.
- `publish` is still tag-only and skips on `site_only`. A `site_only` run cannot make a release page.
- The tag path and the plain dispatch path keep their behaviour: `inputs.site_only` is empty on a push and `false` by default.
- A `site_only` dispatch from `main` builds the site as a check and does not deploy it.

## Test run

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo test -p xtask --test release_site_tests`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --test release_site_tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`), and the job conditions read as above.
- The branch `site/v0.25.0` (site fixes at `3bc320a8c`) passes `python -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: 82 tests OK.

## The same release.yml goes on site/v0.25.0 before the dispatch

GitHub runs a dispatch with the workflow file of the dispatched ref. The tag's `release.yml` has no `site_only` input. Thus `site/v0.25.0` has the `release.yml` of this PR as one commit, `ci(release): site_only dispatch (from PR #3277)` (head `e41d7129f`). That file is byte-identical to the file at this PR's head `b05a95c39`. If this PR changes `release.yml` again, the same file goes on `site/v0.25.0` again before the dispatch.

## Not exercised

- No workflow ran. The dispatch is still owed:
  `gh workflow run release.yml --ref site/v0.25.0 -f site_only=true`
- Owner action first: the `github-pages` environment must permit the branch policy `site/*`. Without it, GitHub refuses the `pages` deploy of the dispatch.

Changelog: none
Process change: yes
Effort: medium

Refs #3276

title: fix(ui): Stock From model applies the part that Source shows

## What changed
- The Stock page Source picker writes the part that it shows into the stock draft. It does this each frame when the two differ.
- Apply now submits the shown part. The user does not have to change Source first.
- A new decision file records the choice: `docs/decisions/3261-stock-source-default.md`.

## Cause
- `source_fields` wrote the name into the draft only when the selection index changed.

- Mutation checks: the seeded harness makes both model-count checks red. The blank harness restores green. The old `stock_page.rs` makes both application pins red. Restoring the fix makes them green.

title: fix(2d): axis start reseats to an exact edge; XY arc entry tries the closing edge
body:
This PR is partial. It fixes two of the three `known-fail #2849` pins. The third pin needs a maintainer decision.

## What changed

- `lead_ext::axis_reseat` keeps the ring start only when the first edge is exactly on X or Y, or when no edge is nearer an axis. Before, it kept the start for each first edge within `axis_tol` (1 degree).
- `descent_xy::plan_xy` tries the first-cut tangent first, as before. When no radius fits and the first pass is a ring that returns to its start, it tries the direction of the closing edge. It uses that direction only within 1e-3 rad of the first-cut tangent.
- The `known-fail #2849` markers of two `lead_approach` pins are removed. Their asserts do not change.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/2849-two-pins.md`.

This is the held work of `issue/2849-three-pins` (`bfc1dc03b`), taken onto the latest main and gated again.

## Cause

- Test 2: the solidcore mesh gives a first edge 0.93 degrees off X. That edge is inside the tolerance, so the start was kept. `entry_arc::true_arc` posts G18/G19 only for an exact axis edge, so the arc was posted as chords.
- Test 1: the arc tangent came from the fitted walk arc. The ring polyline that returns to the start was 0.6 micron off that tangent line. The ring behind the start then crossed the arc hull on both sides, at each radius.

## Tests

- Pins (red on unchanged code, green with the fix):
  - `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`
  - `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`
- Unit pins: `lead_ext::reseat_tests` (2 tests), `descent_xy::closing_tests` (1 test).
- Mutations:
  - Old `lead_ext.rs`: the G18/G19 pin goes red. The other pins stay green.
  - Old `descent_xy.rs`: the horizontal arc pin goes red. The other pins stay green.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green. Steps: motion lib, `motion:xy_arc_entry`, `app:area_open`, `app:lead_approach`.
- Also run and green:
  - motion: `vertical_arc_entry`, `refusal_ghost`, `one_descent`, `level_links`, `entry_arc_3d`, `entry_approach`, `entry_arc`, `blind_floor`, `center_cut_law`, `corner_arc_radius`.
  - app: `wall_arc_entry`, `top_plane_noise`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`, `level_links`, `contour_none_lead`, `arc_entry`, `golden_cl`, `contour_start_point`, `shoulder_adaptive`.
  - post: `vertical_arc_entry`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Final-head checks on `635c0c7bc8c187a92cfcd589aedca9a1597b0efd`:

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green. All 238 steps passed across the reached motion and app heavy lanes.
- Motion heavy tests: 59 passed. App heavy tests: 43 passed.
- All four known-fail checks stayed enabled and failed as expected: three for #1950 and one for #2849.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. All 6 steps passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The review requested test results only. No source change or new commit was needed. The head did not change.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised

- Test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) keeps its marker. A ring order change fixes it, but it makes `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. The two pins want opposite wall orders on a holed area. ## ⚠️ Merge order: not during a cut, and only after the label exists
1. Settings -> Actions -> Runners -> **wopr** -> add the label **`camcraft-cut`**. Optionally add it to `uma` too, as a backup. No re-registration is needed.
2. Then merge this.

If `cut.yml` asks for `camcraft-cut` before any runner has it, the gate waits in the queue forever. For tonight's cut, a stop-gap on the runner owner's side keeps the gate on `wopr`: every other runner is stopped while the release PR is open.

title: fix(wire): allow sharp inside corners at the wire radius
body:
## What changed

- A Wire Contour has a new per-operation option: `sharp_corners`. The default is off.
- Off: the behaviour does not change. A sharp inside corner is refused by name, as before.
- On: the cover law accepts an uncut rest up to the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap). A sharp inside corner of 60 degrees or more keeps no more than that.
- The worst accepted rest is a note on the path (`wire EDM: sharp inside corners stated - ...`).
- The post's wire verify line also says the note. It is not a refusal.
- A rest past the kerf offset is still refused. The message says that the option was on.
- The option is in these places:
  - the project file (`sharp_corners`, absent when off, so old files read unchanged);
  - the wire page, Geometry tab ("Sharp inside corners at the wire radius"), applied by `EditOperationParams`;
  - MCP `edit_operation`, through the params DTO (no new tool is necessary).
- The 4-axis cut does not read the option. It keeps its own `heal_tolerance`.

## Cause

The cover law in `motion::wire_edm::laws` had one rule: each profile point must be within the kerf offset of the wire path. A sharp inside corner always breaks that rule. The report's known-good Sodick program cuts a sharp 10 mm square, and the corner takes the wire radius.

## Tests

- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_when_sharp_inside_corners_are_stated`: a sharp 10 mm square die with k = 0.162 mm. Off is refused with the issue's numbers (0.1620, 0.0671). On is cut, with the note and rest 0.0671. The wire corner stays k from both sides. A punch gets no note.
- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused`: a 30-degree corner stays refused with the option on.
- `app` `wire_sharp_corners::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_and_verified_with_its_corner_rest_as_a_note`: the command path, generation, the verify line, the project round trip, and undo.
- `ui` lib `wire_page_tests::wire_sharp_inside_corners_toggle_applies_and_undoes`: the checkbox, Apply and undo.
- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::a_tapered_sharp_square_die_keeps_its_corner_rest_note` (review fix): a sharp square die with a 1-degree taper keeps the corner-rest note. The note names the top plane and the kerf across the leaning wire.
- `app` `wire_sharp_corners::a_tapered_sharp_square_die_says_its_corner_rest_on_the_verify_line` (review fix): a tapered sharp die generates, verifies with no problem, and the verify line says the rest.
- Mutation (review fix): the taper drops the carried note. The two tapered pins are red. After the restore, they are green.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile (the option did not exist). On unchanged code, the sharp die is refused (the existing test `a_corner_tighter_than_the_wire_is_refused_by_name` pins that).
- Mutation checks (each red, then green after the restore):
  - `sharp_reach` gives 0 when the option is on (the old law): `a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_when_sharp_inside_corners_are_stated` is red.
  - `sharp_reach` has no bound (1e9): `an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused` is red.
  - The verify line does not add the note: `a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_and_verified_with_its_corner_rest_as_a_note` is red.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on head c66edc9ef (merged with upstream main 69c9fd7af): 651 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `example_catalog` `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::{rebuilds,regenerates}`, which passed the 60 s timer limit under a machine load near 50. This change does not touch that code. Alone, the two tests pass in 36 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` on c66edc9ef: clean.

## Heavy and light lanes (head c66edc9ef)

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: the `motion heavy` and `app heavy` lanes, 241 steps, 0 failed, 103.8 min. Six known-fail tests are red as expected (#1950, #2849).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 3 steps, 0 failed.

## Screenshots

The wire page, Geometry tab. After the change, the page has the new row "Sharp inside corners at the wire radius". The default is off.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3232/before-geometry.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3232/after-geometry.png) |

## Goldens moved

None. No `.cl` or `.nc` file changed. The other test changes add `sharp_corners: false` to struct literals only.

## Not exercised

- The open run's own mitre-fold check (`open::offset`) does not change. An open run with a very short segment at a sharp corner can still be refused there.
- The 4-axis cut ignores the option.
- On a tapered cut, the rest is measured on the top plane, where the cover law runs. The note says so. The lower plane has no separate rest reading.
- No run on a real control.

## Overlaps

- The open draft chain #2972, #2974, #2978, #2979, #2981, #2992, #2993 and #2999 adds other fields to the same `WireContourOp` literals in `crates/app/tests/*` and `wire_edm_dto.rs`. It touches the same files, but different fields. Whichever merges second refreshes. Each conflict is two added lines.
- #3205 and #3219 touch `wire_verify.rs`, in different functions.
- #3058 touches `open.rs`, in different functions.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3207-wire-sharp-corners.md`.

Changelog: Wire Contour can accept sharp inside corners at the wire radius (new per-operation option, default off); the corner leftover is said as a note in the path and the verify line.

Fixes #3207

title: fix(sim): judge a wire taper at the model's chord tolerance, refuse an undercut
body:
## What changed

- A constant-taper Wire Contour is judged under the model's chord tolerance. The tolerance is the importer's chord promise (0.005 mm). A model that records a coarser chord uses that chord. 4-axis cuts keep their stated tolerance (#1170).
- The report line and a gouge name "the model's chord tolerance" for such a cut. Stated tolerances keep the old words.
- A new undercut law (`sim/src/verify/wire/undercut.rs`) judges the last pass of a constant-taper cut. A move that cuts a drafted wall at one judged height must cut it at every height. If it stands off the wall past the tolerance at another height, the post is blocked with `wire undercut: the kerf of move N stands ... mm off the part ...`.
- The law skips a move on a vertical wall. A taper on a vertical wall is a stated relief, as in the #536 and #1164 fixtures.
- `WireJob` has a new field `taper_chord`. `WireFinding::Gouge` has a new field `chord`. `WireVerdict` has a new field `chord`. The test literals get `taper_chord: false`.

## Cause

The generator lays the tapered wire from the section at one height. The facets at the other heights stand off the true cone by up to their chord. The kerf law judged those facets with a tolerance of 0, so the true angle was refused. No law read a kerf that stands too far from the wall, so a wrong angle that leaves material passed.

## Tests

- New suite `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_chord.rs`. The fixture is a cone punch with a 128-gon top and a 64-gon base, each inside the chord promise. The base ring is turned half a step.
  - `a_meshed_cone_posts_at_its_true_angle_under_the_chord_tolerance`: red before the fix with `Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 2 enters the part by 0.0007 mm near X-3.499 Y-0.086 at Z0.001 (64 move(s) gouge)`. Green after.
  - `a_taper_past_the_wall_is_refused_as_an_undercut` (5.3 deg on a 5.194 deg wall): red before the fix (the program posted). Green after.
  - `a_taper_short_of_the_wall_still_gouges` (5.1 deg): a guard. Green before and after.
- Mutations, each red, then restored and green:
  - Tolerance 0 for a taper cut again: the true-angle pin and the undercut pin fail.
  - Undercut law not called: the undercut pin fails.
  - Vertical-wall guard removed: `wire_taper::a_tapered_punch_posts_its_golden_and_its_cl_shows_the_poses` fails.
- Suites run green: `camcraft-sim` lib `verify::wire` (20), and app `solid_law_goldens`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_fans`, `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_taper_chord`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol`, `edm_machine`, `mcp_edit_machine`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `setup_align_non_mill`.
- Final checked head: `74c469d186840e201828a7e7c3888ea3683638ea`.
- Merged `upstream/main` at `69c9fd7af`. The merge keeps both added helpers in `wire_verify.rs` unchanged.
- Added `taper_chord: false` to the new upstream depth-test fixture. Before this change, sim library compilation failed with E0063. After this change, all 232 sim library tests passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. All 639 steps completed. 4,449 tests passed; 47 were ignored; no test failed.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: PASS on the final head. All 241 steps completed in 33.6 minutes. No step failed. The motion lane passed 59 tests. The app lane passed 43 tests.
- The heavy gate also confirmed six registered expected failures for #1950 and #2849. The gate accepted these checks. They are not passing product tests.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: PASS on the final head. Both light twins passed. All 3 steps completed in 0.4 minutes. No step failed.
- All checks ran locally. No golden changed. No review evidence was committed.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A real STEP import of the issue's EDM-T3 part. The pins use a synthetic mesh.
- A die (a conical hole). The law reads a die with the same product rule as the kerf law. No pin covers it.
- A model that records a coarser chord. The code reads `model_fidelity::chord_of`, but no pin covers it.
- A real EDM control.
- The optional part of the issue (read the taper angle from a picked wall) is not done.

## Overlaps

These open PRs change other lines of `wire_verdict` in `crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs`: #3219, #3205, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978. This PR changes only the `WireJob` literal lines there, and adds the new function `taper_chord`. The chord is read from the entities, not from the local `material`, which some of those PRs move. The PR is not stacked, because it touches the same file and a different part of the function. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3210-wire-taper-chord.md`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a tapered cut is judged against the model's chord tolerance, so a meshed cone posts at its true angle; a taper that does not follow a drafted wall is refused as an undercut.

Fixes #3210

title: feat(catalog): a catalog case can expect a refusal
body:
Stacked on #3139 (merge #3139 first).

## What changed

- The `expect` field of `case.toml` takes `"post"` or `"refusal"`. Other values are refused by name.
- The 12 existing cases change to `expect = "post"`. #3139 held a free-text description there. The README of each case keeps that text.
- A refusal case has no `<case>.nc`. It has `refusal.txt`: the refusal lines that the script host records, one line each.
- The script of a refusal case saves the project, then runs the refused step without a catch. The script run ends with an error.
- The app tests `regenerates` and `rebuilds` read `expect`:
  - `regenerates` opens the saved project in the script host (`cam.load`, `cam.generate`, `cam.post`). It compares `ScriptOutcome::errors` with `refusal.txt`.
  - `rebuilds` runs `build.camscript` with `camcraft-cli`. It requires a failed exit, a saved project, no `.nc`, and the same lines on stderr.
  - The two tests also open the project and check that its model is embedded, with no file link.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check` accepts a refusal case without a `.nc` file. It runs the script and compares the refusal lines. A refusal case with a `.nc` file fails the layout check.
- `cargo xtask catalog` (rebuild) writes `refusal.txt` for a refusal case.
- New case `2d/drill-overfeed`: an 80 x 50 x 10 mm plate with two 6 mm holes. The Drill feeds at 400 mm/min, above the 115 mm/min of tool DR-0600. The post refuses it by the #2598 clause.
- The 2D operation guide lists the new case under Drill (generated block).
- The catalog README documents `expect` and `refusal.txt`.
- The script host law does not change.

Process change: yes
Effort: high. No escalation.

## Cause

The catalog tests and `--check` required a posted `.nc` for each case. A case could not show a refusal.

## Tests

New pins:

- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::regenerates`
- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::rebuilds`
- `catalog_check_verifies_refusal_case` (xtask integration)

Mutation results (each red, then green after the restore):

1. The app layout and dispatch as before (every case is a post case): the two case tests fail with `2d/drill-overfeed: missing drill-overfeed.nc`.
2. `refusal.txt` says 120 mm/min in place of 115: the two case tests fail with `refusal lines differ from refusal.txt`. `cargo xtask catalog --check` fails with the want/got lines.
3. The refusal case posts (feed lowered to 115 in the script and the project): `regenerates` fails with `the post was not refused`; `rebuilds` fails with `build.camscript ended without an error`.
4. `xtask/src/catalog.rs` from #3139: `catalog_check_verifies_refusal_case` fails with `missing drill-overfeed.nc`.
5. The `expect` value guard removed: `catalog_expect_takes_post_or_refusal_only` fails.
6. The "refusal case has a `.nc`" guard removed: `catalog_layout_accepts_a_refusal_case_without_nc` fails.

Gate:

- The 2 failures are `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::regenerates` and `::rebuilds`: `did not finish within 60s`. The machine load average was 24-30.

title: feat(ui): load machine and post files from the user's disk in the browser
body:
## What changed

The browser build now loads the user's own machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.

- **Load machine (.mch)** and **Load post (.cps)** are live in the browser. They open the browser file picker. A picked machine is mounted. A picked post is selected.
- The Machine page has a new button **Load folder (.mch, .cps)** in the browser build only. It opens `<input webkitdirectory multiple>`. It adds each `.mch` and `.cps` file of the folder to the session lists. It does not need the File System Access API.
- A drop with a `.mch` or `.cps` file goes to a new module `setup_file_drop`. One file is mounted or selected. Several files only join the lists. One status line counts the files that landed and names each refused file with its reason.
- On the desktop, one dropped `.mch` or `.cps` on disk goes to `LoadMachineFile` or `SelectPostFile` by its full path.
- The domain module `camcraft_post::session_files`, re-exported by app, keeps each file by its bare name for the session, on the thread that loaded it. The caller passes app machine validation and holder-aware parsing as a callback. A file enters it only when it passes the checks of a file from disk: a machine must validate and parse, a post must compile and run.
- The readers of machine and post files consult the session store first, then the disk. So `LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile` and the MCP tools run unchanged. Each mount and post choice stays one undo step.
- Session machines show in the machine catalogue (`library::enumerate`). Session posts show in the post combo list.
- A saved project that names a session file which is not loaded again is refused by that name (#2319). There is no fallback.

## Cause

The browser build had no disk and no picker for these files. `browser_files::refusal` greyed Load machine and Load post with `NEEDS_PICKER`. The file drop took model files only. The readers of `PostRef::File` and the machine file read only from disk.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_setup_files.rs`:

- `a_dropped_mch_mounts_by_its_name_and_one_undo_takes_it_away`
- `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes`
- `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_malformed_pick_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `a_picked_folder_fills_both_lists_and_a_picked_file_mounts_or_selects`
- `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` (AccessKit label, role `Button`, enabled state for "Load machine (.mch)", "Load folder (.mch, .cps)" and "Load post (.cps)"; no folder button on the desktop)

Other tests:

- `session_files::tests::a_bad_file_is_refused_by_name_and_never_kept` (post unit test). `an_unloaded_session_post_is_refused_by_name_at_post_time` pins a project that names a file that is not loaded.
- `setup_file_drop::tests::one_file_is_for_its_own_kind_in_any_case`.
- Updated for the new law: `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`.

Red before the fix (reduced pins on unchanged `upstream/main`):

- the drop pins failed with `drop refused: drop-2950-vmc.mch is not a model file (read: .stl, .obj, .step, .stp, .sc, .solidcraft)`;
- the button pin failed with `LoadMachineDialog runs the browser's picker` / `left: Some("Not available in the browser yet: ...")`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pins run, code restored):

- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` from upstream: `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` red.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` from upstream (drop route not called): the three drop pins red.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` from upstream (no session read at post time): `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes` red.
- `session_files::add_post` without its compile check: `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name` red.
- All pins green again after each restore.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 428 steps on the previous head. 427 passed. `ui suites: lib` failed in three machines-pane tests. The cause was a process-global store: the session machines of the new tests leaked into the machine list of tests on other threads.
- The fix makes the store thread-local. The browser runs on one thread.
- On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "app suites: lib" --only "ui suites: lib"` is green (ui lib 1385 passed, 0 failed). Only `crates/app/src/session_files.rs` changed between the two heads, plus one test comment and the decision file. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build. The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed on this machine, so the wasm-only code was not compiled. That code is: the folder input and batch read in `file_pick.rs`, the async drop read in `setup_file_drop.rs`, and the dialog openers in `state_picked.rs`. A reviewer with the target must run `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- A real browser. The tests use `State::browser_build` and in-memory drops as the stand-in.
- Persistence in IndexedDB. Not built. The decision file lists the options for the maintainer.

## Overlaps

- #3057 changes `file_drop::take_drop`. This PR does not change that function. It adds `setup_file_drop::take`, which `shell.rs` calls before `take_drop`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- Several open PRs touch `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in other functions. This PR changes only `script_of`, `resolve_cps` (one line each), the `LoadMachineDialog` / `SelectPostDialog` arms and one new `CommandKind` variant.

## MCP

No new MCP tool. The browser routes go through the existing `LoadMachineFile` and `SelectPostFile` commands, and the MCP machine and post tools read the session store through the same readers. `LoadSetupFolderDialog` is a browser-only picker. It changes no document state.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2950-browser-machine-post-files.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: The browser build loads your own machine (.mch) and post (.cps) files from a picker, a folder picker or a drop; a bad file is refused by name.

Fixes #2950

## Review fixes

- A different post under an existing name is refused. Identical text is accepted. `same_name_folder_and_picker_leave_the_selected_post_and_history_stable` pins the selected post and history.
- One browser batch has a 32 MiB raw-byte limit. Both file lists share a 32 MiB retained-name-and-text limit. Refusals name the file. `individually_allowed_files_cannot_exceed_the_batch_budget` and `retained_text_budget_covers_both_lists_and_refuses_by_name` pin the limits.
- A successful machine import invalidates the machine catalogue. `a_folder_machine_import_invalidates_the_populated_catalogue` starts with a populated catalogue and pins the refreshed list.
- Pure storage and readers belong to `camcraft-post`. App supplies its existing machine checks through a callback. `pure_session_readers_are_available_without_the_app` pins the domain API.

title: feat(ui): show the operator side at the work envelope
body:
## What changed

The viewport now shows the operator side of the work envelope. An arrow starts at the lower edge of the operator-side face. The arrow points out of the envelope, toward the operator. The text "Operator side" is at the tip of the arrow.

- `camcraft-post`: a machine file can state `general.operator_side`. The words are `"-X"`, `"+X"`, `"-Y"` and `"+Y"`. The word names the world axis that points from the envelope to the operator.
  - The field is optional. Old machine files and old projects load without a change.
  - A wrong word refuses the file by name. A wrong word never reads as the default.
  - `OperatorSide::default_for` gives the default of each machine kind: `+Y` for a lathe, `-Y` (the front) for each other kind.
- `camcraft-ui`: `operator_side.rs` builds the arrow when its input changes (the placed envelope and the side). Each other frame reads the kept arrow. The text is screen text, so it stays readable when the view turns.
- The View door has a new box, "Show operator side". It is view state: on by default, no command, not saved. It is disabled while the work envelope is off.
- The arrow and the text use the envelope colour. They are outside the envelope, so they do not cover the part or the toolpath.
- Docs: `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the machine file grammar) and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md` (the defaults for each kind).

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for. The viewport did not show from which side the operator looks into the work envelope.

## Before and after screenshots

Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted and the work envelope shown. The camera looks from the front. "Before" is the same scene with the new box off. With the box off, the scene is the same as on `upstream/main`.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-after.png) |

The screenshots are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. A temporary collector made them. The collector is not in this branch.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/post/tests/operator_side.rs`:

- `an_old_file_without_the_field_loads_and_takes_the_default_of_its_kind` (also loads each library `.mch` file)
- `each_kind_has_its_documented_default_side`
- `a_file_that_names_a_side_keeps_it_over_the_default`
- `a_wrong_word_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `a_stored_machine_without_the_field_still_reads_and_a_stated_side_round_trips`

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/operator_side.rs`:

- `a_mill_shows_the_arrow_and_the_text_on_its_default_side`
- `each_machine_kind_shows_the_arrow_on_its_default_side`
- `a_lathe_shows_the_arrow_on_the_viewer_side_of_the_turning_plane` (checks the cylinder surface and outward direction for the default and all four stated sides)
- `a_machine_that_names_a_side_moves_the_arrow_to_it` (also through the file text)
- `no_envelope_means_no_arrow_and_no_text`
- `the_switch_hides_and_shows_the_arrow_and_the_text_as_view_state`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_arrow_and_a_changed_input_builds_one` (the frame-cost counter test)

The pins do not compile on `upstream/main`, because the types are new. Mutation checks, each restored after the run:

1. The parser does not read `general.operator_side`: 2 post pins go red.
2. The scene draws the envelope without the arrow: 3 UI pins go red.
3. The cache builds the arrow again on each frame: the counter pin goes red.
4. The draw ignores the "Show operator side" box: the switch pin goes red.
5. The lathe uses the old anchor at the corner of its bounding box: the lathe surface pin goes red at `[-60, 60, -97]`. Restore the cylinder projection: the pin passes (1 passed).

Final-head verification (`9cf25fd20db55a3198b53180cdcb64644c222b25`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 96 steps passed in 12.2 minutes. Test totals: 2,311 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green in 136.0 minutes. All 204 steps completed (1 release build and 203 app heavy target steps). There were 44 passed tests and 2 expected failures (#1950 and #2849). The gate accepted both expected failures. No unexpected failures occurred.
- `cargo clippy -j2 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed in 17 minutes 54 seconds.

The shared sccache did not answer. The final gate runs use `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

title: fix(slot): cut the round ends of a slot wider than the tool
body:
## What changed

- A Slot wider than its tool now runs one wall lap at each level, after the rows.
- The lap follows the boundary of the tool centre stadium: two straight sides and two half circles.
- Each half circle is a chain of arcs (G02/G03). The chain is split at every row end on it and at its tip, so no arc is more than 90 degrees.
- The rows and the lap compute a row end with one function (`cap_point`). Each row join meets the lap at the same point to the bit.
- The lap starts where the last row ends and closes at that point.
- Under `climb` the lap is counterclockwise (the slot's air on the left, the same sense as the rows). Under conventional it is clockwise.
- A full-width slot (`h = 0`, one row on the centre line) does not change.
- The lap code is in the new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_lap.rs`. `slots.rs` is 394 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2906-slot-round-ends.md`.

## Cause

A row touches a round end only at its end point. The move between two rows is a straight line. The tool did not follow the arc between two row ends. On a 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool, 0.86 mm stayed on the wall of each round end.

## Why the arcs are split at the row ends

The first version used two quarter arcs for each cap. The quick gate refused it on 8 app suites. The verifier's crossing law (a) flattens an arc into chords inside its circle. A row join is a chord that ends exactly on the circle, so it crossed those flattened chords, and the post was held. With the split, the join and the lap share their vertices. The law reads a shared vertex as a touch, not a crossing. The crossing law does not change.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_climb`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_conventional`
  - `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends`
  - Each point on the stadium wall must be within the tool radius of the tool centre path (limit 0.01 mm). No tool centre point may leave the cutter centre stadium. `crossed_pairs` (the verifier's crossing law) must be empty.
  - Red before the fix: `climb=true z=9: 0.855 mm left on the wall at (28.536, 18.536)`.
- New unit tests in `slot_lap.rs`: the lap closes on its start; each row end is a lap vertex; CCW from `b` runs the +n side first; CW from `b` turns round `b` first.
- Mutations repeated on head `35020f6cc294c3b6266be720b3c9d2b178c970f9`:
  - Disable the wall lap: all three `slot_round_ends` tests fail. The climb and conventional tests leave 0.855 mm on the wall. Restore the source: all three tests pass.
  - Remove the row-end splits: `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends` fails its crossing assertion. Restore the source: all three tests pass.
  - Both restorations match the reviewed source byte for byte. The worktree has no source changes.
- Expected-change test updates:
  - `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`: `slot_offsets_rows_across_a_wide_channel`, `conventional_slot_starts_at_the_far_end`, `slot_stock_to_leave_narrows_the_center_area` read the rows as the prefix of the level and pin the lap (arc count, direction, tips at x = -7 and 47, close at the last row end). `slot_helix_orbits_in_the_certified_channel` counts only descending arcs as the helix.
  - `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` (`an_entry_edit_marks_the_slot_stale_and_the_orbit_proves_itself`): an orbit is a descending arc. The planar arcs are the lap.
  - `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_2d_slots.rs`: the Slot now has 8 arc blocks (4 for each level).
  - `crates/app/tests/clearance_in_stock.rs` (`a_slot_traverse_at_a_clearance_plane_inside_the_stock_is_convicted_and_holds_the_post`): see "Side effect" below.

## Final-head validation

Head: `35020f6cc294c3b6266be720b3c9d2b178c970f9`. No new commit was needed for this validation request.

Base: `upstream/main` at `a35c9cb8197f484fca0f8311610bdc8594111a0f`. The diff merge base is `11402dba4c849c5f827dccebc14f850196614311`.

- The failed test is `adaptive_troch_parallel::wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes`. It takes 123.369 seconds against a 90-second debug limit. No geometry assertion fails.
- The isolated failed-step retry uses `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=1`. Its one gate step passes; both tests pass. The suite takes 107 seconds.
- The CL and post fixture readers pass. The changed golden readers pass.

- App `clearance_in_stock` and `solid_law_goldens` pass.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: exit 0. All 235 steps complete in 109.1 minutes, with zero unexpected failures. Both reached lanes, motion and app, run in full.
- Reached motion lane: 37 steps, 57 tests pass, 2 expected failures reproduce.
- Reached app lane: 197 steps, 43 tests pass, 4 expected failures reproduce. The shared build is the remaining step.
- Six known-fail tests produce their expected red results. The gate accepts these expected results.
- Motion heavy library tests: 8 pass. Motion `finish3d`: 33 pass.
- App heavy `operations`: 6 pass. App `rotary_field_parity`: 6 pass in 864.35 seconds.

title: fix(kernel): measure a fan at a spline pole by its true sag
body:
## Problem and change

A closed STEP solid can have a spline face that ends at a pole. The old deviation measure can reject its valid mesh.

`mesh_pole::settle` moves the free parameter at a pole to the mean of the other two triangle corners. It uses one side of the period. It keeps the move only when the surface point stays within 1e-9 mm. `mesh_deviation::face` applies this step before it samples a spline triangle. Analytic faces keep their existing path. The deviation bounds do not change.

The PR includes two original fixtures:

- `testdata/models/sphere_quarter_pole.step`: a quarter sphere, R 25, with a rational B-spline dome and an apex pole.
- `testdata/models/q02_3d_mold.step`: the recorded SolidCraft QA part from #3034. The file has 347101 bytes. SHA256: `111862a3c03262db764d92e63c5c32f384541b14840d494f6bf3bf4fc5bb9567`.

Both fixtures have STEP agreement rows and named tests. No HSMWorks source or assets were used.

## Cause and readings

The issue reports an open mesh on v0.24.0. On upstream/main `8be100737`, the import itself refused q02:

```text
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 10 is the ellipsoid boss (`#3666`), with a pole at its top. Its mesh sag is about 0.004 mm. The old measure interpolated the free parameter across half the period. Its projection hint was then on the far side of the surface. A finer chord did not reduce the measured bound.

With the fix, the recorded q02 file imports with 48780 facets and no open edges. Its signed volume is 97163.50 mm^3. SolidCraft reports 97165.69 mm^3. The test allows 10 mm^3.

The slice at z = 19.6875, the reported height, has area 1382.27 mm^2. Slices at z = 18.5, 20, 25 and 29 also close. The test checks the measured areas within 0.5 mm^2.

## Regression pins

- Kernel `mesh_deviation_pole::a_fan_at_a_spline_pole_measures_by_its_true_sag`.
- Kernel `mesh_deviation_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_meshes_inside_the_tolerance`.
- App `import_step_spline_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_imports_closed_and_slices`.
- Kernel lib `mesh_pole::tests` (3 tests).
- App `import_step_q02_mold::the_recorded_q02_mould_imports_closed_and_slices_at_the_reported_height`.
- App `import_step_q02_mold::the_recorded_q02_mould_generates_a_3d_flat_finish` (heavy lane).

The q02 generation pin uses the full recorded model and the normal undoable generation command. It uses Flat Finish3D, BN-0600, top z = 30 mm, bottom z = 18 mm, stepover 2 mm, and tolerance 0.05 mm. It checks finite moves and more than 10 mm of horizontal Feed on the base at z = 18 mm. The initial release run passed: 1 test, 8.27 s. The final-head heavy run also passed this pin: 1 test, 7.90 s.

Mutation check on this follow-up:

- Restored `mesh_deviation.rs` from upstream/main: RED, exit 101, in 5.19 s. The new q02 generation pin refused the import with the original diagnostic:

```text
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

- Restored the fix byte for byte: GREEN, 1 test passed in 7.88 s. The restored file has no diff.

## Final-head validation

Head: `d3df8a0256a5b768c0d21e4034acf0c0f8c34fd4`.
Base: upstream/main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, exit 0. All 91 steps passed in 22.6 minutes. Tests: 2214 passed, 0 failed, 32 ignored. The q02 generation pin is in the heavy lane. The direct release run above passed it.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, exit 0. All 253 reached steps completed in 55.9 minutes. No unexpected step failed. Tests: 105 passed, 6 tracked expected failures, 0 ignored. Kernel: 4 passed. Motion: 57 passed and 2 expected failures. App: 44 passed and 4 expected failures.
- `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, exit 0, in 1 minute 21 seconds.

The gate accepts the six tracked expected failures below. They are not passing tests.

| Crate | Test | Tracked issue |
|---|---|---|
| motion | `ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock` | #1950 |
| motion | `ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note` | #1950 |
| app | `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` | #1950 |
| app | `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19` | #2849 |
| app | `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent` | #2849 |
| app | `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` | #2849 |

## Limits

The 3D generation pin covers a Flat finish of the base at z = 18 mm. It keeps the full recorded model. Earlier broad Waterline and Parallel attempts did not finish. They are not passing generation results. The PR does not claim that all 3D strategies complete on q02.

The 1e-9 mm point check in `settle` has no separate pin. No constructed surface has a zero derivative at a point that is not a pole.

No goldens or UI source changed. No screenshots are required for this diff.

Changelog: A closed STEP solid with a spline face that ends in a pole (for example an ellipsoid or a dome from SolidCraft) now imports. Before, the import refused it with "stands ... mm off its surface".

Fixes #3034

title: fix(2d): read a drafted side as a wall, not as a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

- A no-pick 2D chamfer now reads a drafted side as a wall. It does not read it as a modelled chamfer.
- The chamfer takes a third section of the material, half way between the top plane and the corner plane.
- A piece of a top loop is a drafted wall when two conditions are true:
  - It stands off the wall by no more than `depth * tan(15 deg)`.
  - The corresponding half-depth wall covers the expected segment along the whole piece within `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm).
- A loop with drafted pieces and no bevelled piece rides its wall at the corner depth. It counts with the sharp loops (#2596). Thus a plate with no modelled chamfer breaks every edge, the drafted side and the pocket included.
- The half-depth loop matches the corner wall by winding and the smallest symmetric whole-loop vertex gap. Each piece requires full coverage by parallel segments with the same direction. Collinear section vertices are allowed.
- `partly_bevelled` becomes `read`, which returns a `Reading`. The #2887 refusal text does not change.
- `ride_loops` takes two new arguments: `mid` (the half-depth section) and `depth`. The one caller, `material_source.rs`, makes the half-depth section.

## Cause

PR #2894 refuses a loop that is bevelled on only part of its length. It reads each piece more than 0.05 mm off the wall as "bevelled". A drafted side also stands off the wall. With a 1 mm chamfer and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is more than 0.05 mm off. The plate was refused with a "modelled chamfer" message.

Two sections cannot tell a draft from a small modelled chamfer. A third section checks the straight slope within the section grid slack. A draft puts the half-depth section at half the offset. A modelled chamfer that ends before the corner plane departs from this slope. The review found that a 25% residual allowance admitted a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The check now uses `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm). A later review found that one matching midpoint or an unrelated hole could excuse a partial bevel. The check now requires continuous coverage on the corresponding wall along the whole piece.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride_tests.rs`:

- `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall`: #2887's plate with its X0 side drafted 3.5, 5 and 10 degrees. Red on unchanged code: `the edge loop near X0.087 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length`.
- `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft`: a 0.2 mm modelled bevel on one side is still refused.
- `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: the review fixture has a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The test requires the partial-bevel refusal for a 1 mm ride.
- `a_side_whose_slope_turns_back_is_no_draft`: a side that turns back at half depth is refused.
- `half_depth_must_match_along_the_whole_piece`: a slanted half-depth wall that matches only at the midpoint is refused.
- `an_unrelated_mid_depth_hole_must_not_excuse_a_bevel`: a buried hole cannot supply the outer wall match.
- `a_drafted_side_allows_collinear_half_depth_vertices`: a straight draft still passes with extra collinear section vertices.
- `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer`: a 45 degree bevel deeper than the ride is still refused.
- The #2887 tests (`a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `..._with_an_extra_vertex_too`) still pass. The old test calls go through a small `ride` helper.

Mutation checks (each guard taken out, then put back):

- Drafted reading off: `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall` red.
- Half-depth check off: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` red.
- Slope limit off: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` red.
- Drafted match arm after the vertex-gap arm: the 3.5 degree case of the drafted pin red (it rode the top loop, inside the part).

Verification on head `b582f0cf12ab38fa1d9f2d7a0c7d4be13db241c4`:

- Both new refusal pins fail with the prior head behavior restored (RED). Both pass with the fix restored (GREEN).
- All 21 `chamfer_ride` library tests pass, including the collinear positive pin.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 139 steps pass. Tests: 1943 passed, 0 failed, 64 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: GREEN. Both steps pass. Tests: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 235 steps pass in 38.2 minutes. Every reached motion and app target ran, with no manual skips. Tests: 57 motion and 43 app; 100 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Six expected-failure validations were verified: two motion and four app.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No app-level test with a real drafted STEP or STL model. The pins use hand-built sections.
- A drafted side under a tilted frame. The check measures along the frame's lean, but no test covers it.

## Overlaps

PRs #3058, #2836 and #2714 touch `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs`. They change other match arms, not the `Chamfer2D` arm. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2929-chamfer-drafted-side.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges no longer refuses a part with a drafted side as a partly bevelled edge loop; the drafted side is chamfered along its wall.

Fixes #2929

title: fix(motion): Circular climbs to clearance between its rings
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: before each ring after the first, the tool climbs straight up to clearance at the end of the last ring. Then the ring's ladder enters from clearance, as the first ring does. This applies to the flat mode and to the vault.
- The unit tests of `circular.rs` move to `circular_tests.rs` with no change. This keeps `circular.rs` at 361 lines (it was 411 before this PR).
- Two goldens gain the one new climb move.
- New pins in `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`.

## Cause

Each ring runs its own level ladder (ring-major order). The first descent of a ladder expects the tool at clearance. After the first ring, the tool stood on that ring's floor. The descent then made one diagonal rapid from the floor up to clearance over the next ring's start. That rapid crossed the core that the next ring had still to cut. Verification convicted it and held the post. A 5 mm hole with a Ø6 tool has only one ring, so the catalog case did not show the fault. The vault had the same diagonal rapid.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_link_between_circular_rings_clears_the_stock` (motion): plunge, helix and ramp entry; planar and default links; flat and vault. No lateral rapid under the stock top. The verifier convicts no rapid.
- `the_issue_case_climbs_to_clearance_between_its_rings` (motion): the issue's four rings (R 7, 5, 3, 1). Each traverse onto R 5, 3 and 1 is at clearance.
- `a_spliced_diagonal_link_between_rings_is_still_convicted` (motion): the real path is clean. A diagonal link of the old shape, spliced in, gets `RapidInStock`. This is the "post stays blocked for a deliberately unsafe link" part of Done.
- `a_multi_ring_circular_links_its_rings_over_the_stock_and_posts` (app): the issue's job through generate, verify and post. No warning, and the program posts, for the plunge and the ramp entry.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the app pin reports `RapidInStock { at: 69 }` and `RapidInStock { at: 119 }`, the moves that the issue names. The motion pin reports rapids under the stock top at moves 69, 119 and 169.

Mutation: the fix with the climb disabled makes all three motion pins red (the flat case and the vault case at moves 20 and 40). The fix restored makes them green.

Gate:

Verification head: `050d1a7051475c6634e7493b6c8aa7077a959eeb`.
Invocation base: `upstream/main` at `1d5de9aeb846b83ee69a6cbbfd6f2ee8cdd3230e`.
The effective diff merge base was `0b8f4879dd88afe5f658a18c5dde035a88be41e3`.
These runs tested the unchanged final head directly.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green. All 240 steps passed in 45.3 minutes.
- Every reached motion heavy target ran. Its 37 steps had 59 ordinary test passes and two accepted expected-failure controls for #1950.
- Every reached app heavy target ran. Its 202 steps had 44 ordinary test passes and two accepted expected-failure controls for #1950 and #2849.
- One shared release build completes the 240 heavy steps. No unexpected failure occurred.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. All 705 steps passed in 42.1 minutes.
- Motion `circular_ring_links`: all four tests passed, including `a_multi_ring_helix_keeps_both_the_clearance_lift_and_descent_tracking`.
- App `circular_ring_links`: its generation, verification, and posting test passed.
- `default_machine_missing`: all nine tests passed, including `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green in 33 seconds.
- Heavy used a job budget of 24. Quick used eight jobs and `CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off` while heavy ran concurrently.
- Clippy ran with quick after heavy finished. No tracked file changed during verification.
- Another session advanced the local main reference after both gate plans started. The invocation base above applies to both runs.
- The latest finding required verification evidence. No source edit, new pin, or new mutation check was needed.

## Goldens moved

Two goldens. Each gains one line, `Rapid <x> <y> <clearance>`, at the first ring's end, with the same X and Y. The header move count goes up by one. No other line changes.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ring_arcs.cl`: 401 to 402 moves.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ramp_stay_down.cl`: 133 to 134 moves.

## Not exercised

- The helix entry with several rings is still refused. Each ring's helix touches the last ring's helix at the start of the ring, in the same depth band. The crossing law convicts that touch. The program is refused, not unsafe. Follow-up: #3109.
- I tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode on this branch. It removed the helix crossings, but the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. I dropped it (see the decision record).
- Pixel snapshots were not run.
- This verification used the configured sccache wrapper at `/home/mikekinney/.local/bin/sccache`.

## Overlaps

- #2842 changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs` too, in the level ladder calls (`cut_levels_under`, `levels_from`). This PR changes the lines before `run_level_walks` and moves the test module. Touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Circular with several rings no longer links its rings with a rapid through the stock; each ring after the first climbs to clearance first, so verification passes and the program posts.

Effort: high
