title: fix(3d): an Adaptive fallback to Offset rings raises a warning
body:
Stacked on #3062 (merge #3062 first).

This PR is partial work on #3035. It does the warning part only.

## What changed

- `camcraft_sim::verify::Warning` has a new variant, `StrategyFallback { at, areas }`.
  - It is advisory. `blocks_post` is false.
  - `at` is the first cutting move. `areas` is the number of areas that the Offset rings cut in place of the Adaptive plan.
- Generate (`operation/generate.rs`) counts the fallback notes and adds the warning when the count is more than zero.
  - The op now reports `warnings` > 0 in MCP `get_job` and `generate`.
  - MCP `verify` lists the finding as `strategy_fallback` with `blocks_post: false`.
  - The UI folds the warning on its own key (225).
- `machining2d::RINGS_FALLBACK` holds the note tail `" - Offset rings cut "`. The 2D door (`pocket_hsm`) and the 3D ladder (`machining3d::hsm::rings_tag`) both use it. `machining2d::rings_fallbacks` counts the notes by it. The note text does not change.
- The rest pass and the offset shells are not counted. Their Offset rings are by design, not a fallback.

## Cause

The planner wrote each fallback to Offset rings only into the path notes. The op status stayed `ok` with `warnings=0`. In the QA run, 14 levels fell back and nothing showed it except the notes.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `app strategy_fallback::an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning` (new). Before the fix it failed: `one fallback warning: []`, left 0, right 1.
  - `motion lib machining3d::hsm::fallback_tests::a_refused_level_counts_as_one_rings_fallback` (new).
- Mutations:
  - `generate.rs` from upstream/main (no guard): the app pin is red. Restored: green.
  - `rings_fallbacks` that matches nothing: the motion pin is red. Restored: green.
- Expected changes: these suites pinned "verifies clean" as zero warnings on fixtures that already fall back to rings. Each now allows only the fallback warning, and only when the notes name a fallback:
  - `adaptive_pinch`
  - `adaptive_zero_margin_island` (the MCP `findings` check skips `strategy_fallback` only)
  - `climb_direction`
  - `shoulder_adaptive`
- Historical quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 313 steps, zero failures. Sim, motion, app and UI pass. The UI library passes. Duration: 65.6 minutes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Warning display screenshots

The images show the real operation properties page for the Milling-test channel fixture.
The capture uses the same parameters as `an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning`.
Before omits only the new advisory from the generated cache to reproduce the previous display.
After uses the exact generated cache. The moves and path notes are the same.
The temporary capture assertions passed. No capture code or images are on this PR branch.

Before: `OK · 73 moves`.

![Warning display before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/41f8ad4764cce2abb6eb9905576b14fb1d84eeb7/3108/warning-before.png)

After: `OK · 73 moves · 1 warning`, with the expanded Adaptive fallback advisory.

![Warning display after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/41f8ad4764cce2abb6eb9905576b14fb1d84eeb7/3108/warning-after.png)

## Author review fixes

Head: `9562dd2adc3f0cb36a90d7103fb1eb6c5a84f039`.

The first full heavy run found six stale warning assertions. The fixes change tests only.
Each guard requires the warning count to match the fallback notes.
Each guard accepts only `StrategyFallback`, with the same area count and `blocks_post: false`.
The geometry checks and configured known-failure assertions remain unchanged.

The six pins are:

- `adaptive_pinch::the_users_part_with_default_adaptive_keeps_the_cutter_off_it`
- `pick_agnostic::a_face_with_an_island_and_its_rim_loop_cut_the_same_bytes_around_the_boss_full`
- `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`
- `shoulder_adaptive::containment_outside_clears_past_the_edge_never_the_recess`
- `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`
- `whole_model_pocket::a_whole_part_adaptive_at_the_default_load_keeps_the_full_tool_radius_off_the_part`

Mutation check: remove the warning insertion from `generate.rs`.
All six pins fail at the warning guard: zero actual warnings, one expected warning.
Restore the source byte for byte: the targeted heavy gate passes nine steps.
The two affected known-failure tests reach their original configured failure reasons.
The selector also includes two unchanged lead-approach known-failure checks.

## Final verification

Verified head: `19a736d203de3ff590de1caea27a74e951966b6c`.
The head is unchanged. This review request required verification only.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: **PASS**, 241 steps, zero gate failures, 59.2 minutes.
  Base at plan creation: `9e8e2135cd4cc580ccb91dfd2ec504c16c9950c7`.
  The gate reached all motion and app heavy targets.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **PASS**, 343 steps, zero failures, no retries, 53.1 minutes.
  Base at plan creation: `0aad72f8825de7a3871b42eea05dbe98a68788a6`.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **PASS**.

Another session advanced the shared `upstream/main` reference between the gate starts.
Each gate selected its tests from the base recorded above. The tested head did not change.
The compile cache stalled before the heavy gate started. The completed runs used the cache disabled.

| Heavy lane | Ordinary tests passed | Configured known-failure tests with expected reasons | Unexpected failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Motion | 59 | 2 | 0 |
| App | 44 | 2 | 0 |

The motion known-failure checks reach their configured stock-ring reasons (#1950).
The app known-failure checks reach their configured bore fallback (#1950) and shoulder clearance (#2849) reasons.
All six warning guards listed above ran in the full heavy gate.
No configured known-failure check failed for a different reason.

| Quick lane | Tests passed | Failed | Ignored |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sim | 467 | 0 | 1 |
| Motion | 1163 | 0 | 58 |
| App | 1757 | 0 | 27 |
| UI | 1440 | 0 | 7 |

The UI library passed 1409 tests. The UI operations suite passed 31 tests.
The worktree stayed clean. No source change, new pin, or mutation was needed for this verification request.
No golden, screenshot, log, or review artifact is on this PR branch.


## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. The posted G-code does not change.

## Not exercised

- The QA part of #3035 (the mould core STL on len) did not run.
- Two parts of #3035 stay open:
  - the run time of Rough12, Rest6 and Waterline6 (5 to 13 min, or more);
  - a long generate that blocks every other MCP call, with no cancel tool.

## Overlaps

- #3062: the same function (`fold_warnings_located`, `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.
- #3080 and #2714 touch `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`, different variants and arms. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3103, #3033 and #2836 touch `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, other functions. #2836 adds `UndercutLift` on key 222; this PR uses 225.
- Many open PRs touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. This PR adds 7 lines after the drill-size law.

Effort: max (this part is smaller; the rest of #3035 stays at its label).

Changelog: An Adaptive operation that falls back to Offset rings now shows a warning with the number of areas, not only a note; the post is not held.

Refs #3035

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 4bd091166. This head merges `upstream/main` at 2d98d87be and adds the `strategy` field to main's new Bore literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 724 steps, 0 failed (113.0 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: equal_steps` and `app suites: bore_helical`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 240 steps (202 app heavy, 37 motion heavy, 1 build), 0 failed (63.8 min). The 6 known-fail steps (#1950, #2849) are red as expected.
- The earlier head c70e84309 had a quick gate of 687 steps and a heavy run of 231 steps, all green.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2b95e5701. `upstream/main` merged in at 2d98d87be.

Fixes #2830

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: feat(ui): place DXF profiles on the stock from the Stock page and a drop
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:
  - "Profile X", "Profile Y" and "Profile angle (deg)". These are a draft. "Place profile" queues one `MoveSketch`.
  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `camcraft_geometry::dxf`, so the UI can name the `Primitive` variants. This adds no crate dependency.

The import does not use `finish_import`. That function handles the model worker. `ImportDxf` checks the drawing at construction, so the typed `DxfUnitsMissing` error is caught where the UI builds the command. `docs/decisions/1863-dxf-stock-ui.md` records this and the other choices.

## Cause

The #1862 commands had no UI door. A user could place a DXF profile only through MCP or the script.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/dxf_profile.rs`:

- `the_stock_page_adds_lists_places_and_deletes_a_dxf_profile`
- `a_drawing_without_units_asks_millimeters_or_inches_and_never_guesses`
- `a_dropped_dxf_lands_on_the_stock_or_asks_for_one`
- `the_browser_lists_the_profile_under_its_stock_with_an_eye`
- `the_viewport_draws_the_chains_on_the_stock_top_and_marks_open_ends`
- `the_operation_page_takes_the_profile_as_its_source_without_a_model`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_profile_lines_and_a_move_builds_once`

Also:

- `page_layout_windows::layout_window_dxf_units` (the named layout test of the new modal).
- `dxf_units_dialog::tests::readings_state_both_units_both_ways`.
- `dxf_drop::tests::dxf_by_extension_in_any_case`.

Red before the fix: yes. On upstream/main the pins do not compile. `CommandKind::ImportDxf`, `CommandKind::MoveSketch`, `State::dxf_units_prompt`, `Leaf::Sketch`, `sketch_overlay` and `op_source` do not exist.

Mutation checks (each red with the mutation, green when restored):

- Guess millimeters for a drawing without units: `a_drawing_without_units...` is red ("nothing lands before the answer").
- Remove the stock check of the drop: `a_dropped_dxf...` is red (the refusal does not name the file).
- Remove the profiles from the Source list: `the_operation_page...` is red.
- Draw a hidden profile: `the_viewport_draws...` is red.
- Bypass the line cache: `a_still_frame_builds...` is red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on `4543f6207be39f2222ad0de0194f469c3296c309` (20 steps, 0 failed: app lib, ui lib and 17 ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code, CL file or snapshot PNG changes.

## Not exercised

- Before and after screenshots are attached below. The captures use the real offscreen renderer. The structural tests pin the labels, the rows and the overlay vertices.
- A `.dxf` dropped in the browser build (wasm) is refused by name. The browser drop path delivers model bytes only.
- The native file picker of "Add DXF profile…" is not driven in a test. The test calls the same `CommandKind::ImportDxf`.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978, #2974, #2972, #2969, #2968, #2964, #2955, #2951, #2786, #2773, #2763, #2932. This PR adds enum variants, two fields and four dispatch arms only.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/stock_page.rs`: #2773 (stock axis). This PR adds one line in `stock_page`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_tree.rs`: #2714. This PR adds a variant to `Leaf` and rows in `setup_children`.
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`: #2932 (a constant). This PR adds one line in `collect_overlay`.

title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**This first writer now uses the zero-step encoder from #3104. The machine template and standalone encoder have merged. The maintainer checked the conflict resolution on `bf4f3edaf` and found no code blocker. The dependency and reference-source decisions remain open.** Later feature drafts still need their own safety review before they can introduce machining behavior. A stale controller quality can change the effective finish, pass count and offsets.

PR #2948 supplied the machine template for issue #2946. PR #3104 supplied the standalone encoder. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This PR retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

On the corrected writer, the normal CLI produced the same three CCSEP20 files as the independently verified import in #3104. Only the output stem was changed from the PUNCH40 example. The copy of the actual control showed the closed punch at zero steps. FORMALCHECK blocked it until the operator assigns technology. See [the file hashes and native work details](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3104#issuecomment-7055077111). The native bytes were tested once in that replay. No physical cut was made.

On successive imports, select the newly created piece. Match its ISO, start hole and zero steps to the intended setup. Verify the effective wire, height, quality and offsets before assigning TECCUT. Run the control's graphic and formal checks on the resulting steps.

On the earlier writer, the control plotted a rough pass and three trims after automatic generation. The measured offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. That historical result does not qualify an automatic release on this or another installation.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Refresh on `31ee72c80`

Merge `31ee72c80ef016be904d1803163898d395724918` joins the previous head `bf4f3edafb6d67a74e6173f673ab6585f0238075` and upstream `1d5de9aeb846b83ee69a6cbbfd6f2ee8cdd3230e`. Git merged them without manual changes. The previous quick gate failed only in `slot_dxf_sketch`. Upstream fix `4c11e92b7` updates its expected slot path from 9 moves to 15.

The scoped author gate passed all 76 tests, including the four slot tests and three desktop Post tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for the app, geometry, post and UI crates. On this head, the full quick gate passed all 1,079 steps in 99.4 minutes. The heavy gate passed all 258 steps in 67.8 minutes. It ran the release build and the kernel, motion and app heavy suites. Both commands used base `1d5de9aeb` and exited with status 0. A trial merge with upstream main at `174584111` completed without conflicts.

The rebuilt CLI reproduced every `PUNCH40` file and the complete zero-step receipt. Changing only the job name to `CCSEP20` reproduced all three files from the earlier offline control check. Both repeat exports preserved the original files. The unconfigured Agie template refused the missing `AGIE_QN2` condition.

The maintainer decision on the direct dependencies still precedes the independent safety review. The Agie-CAM reference decision also remains with the maintainer.

## Refresh after v0.25.0

Merge `bf4f3edafb6d67a74e6173f673ab6585f0238075` brings upstream `5c8340b81` into the reviewed head `f92e67857`. The only conflict was in `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. The test checks wrapped header notes for Klartext, counts all 20 text posts, and checks the Agie refusal for single-file output.

The contributor ran 72 tests on the merge. All passed, including the three desktop Post tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for the app, geometry, post and UI crates. The [maintainer review](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2951#pullrequestreview-6010212258) accepted the conflict resolution. It requested the full quick gate and the reached heavy lanes before the ready flag. Both contributor runs used `bf4f3edaf` with base `5c8340b81`. The full heavy gate passed all 259 steps in 64.0 minutes and exited with status 0. The full quick gate completed all 1,072 steps. Of these, 1,071 passed, including strict Clippy. One slot DXF test failed against the old expected output on this branch. Its actual output matched the corrected reference in [upstream PR #3285](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3285) byte for byte. The [issue record](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2945#issuecomment-7076541271) tracks the refresh.

The normal CLI wrote all three `PUNCH40` files byte for byte as before. Changing only the job name to `CCSEP20` reproduced the files from the earlier offline control check. Both receipts reported zero working steps. Both repeat exports refused to overwrite their destinations. The unconfigured Agie template refused the missing `AGIE_QN2` condition.

The contributor fork synced at the v0.25.0 cut. A trial merge with upstream main at `4d6b75e77` passed. Only the test needed a manual resolution.

## Review changes on `f92e67857`

Commit `25e783b50` merged upstream main at `6fafa4e1f` into the contributor branch. GitHub reports the corrected head as mergeable. A local trial merge with upstream `60cb97a0b` also completed without conflicts.

On `45d6166e1`, 67 focused tests passed. Three desktop tests use the Post button and the synthetic punch. The success case checks the requested finish, all three output files and the zero-step control review. Each refusal case checks that the output directory stays empty.

- `native_post_dialog_writes_three_files_and_reports_the_required_work_checks`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_an_invalid_job_name_without_writing_files`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_per_operation_output_without_writing_files`

On that revision the quick gate passed 1,032 of 1,033 steps, including clippy. All 253 reached heavy steps passed. The only failed step was `post suites: comment_escape`. Its registry test expected a single text file from every post.

The final commit changes only `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. The test checks header escaping for all 19 text posts and checks the native directory refusal for Agie. On `f92e67857`, all 27 focused tests passed. The official quick replay selected the one failed step and passed it. The screenshot source, UI tests and production code are identical on these two revisions.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 6fafa4e1f
# On f92e67857, use the quick log directory from the first command.
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f --failed <original-quick-log-directory>
```

## Checks on reviewed revision `025ed4760` and its predecessors

At a08c802b6, all five writer tests, four standalone encoder tests and ten application integration tests passed. The normal PUNCH40 script reproduced the previous guarded ISO, SBR and SBL. A repeat export refused to replace them. Both PUNCH40 and the CCSEP20 variant returned `working_steps_generated=false` and the controller review.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib agie::tests::
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native
```

Pinning tests include `script_post_reports_the_required_control_review_and_zero_working_steps`, `stock_origin_and_fractional_setup_coordinates_are_refused_before_publication`, `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch` and `qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition`.

The earlier guarded head was 5bdbb5fe4. It includes the upstream diagnostic fix from #3092 and a dedicated recorded-stream suite for the Agie dispatcher. The single-file post entry point must refuse the Agie dispatcher. Each of 11 input streams checks the diagnostic, the failure exit code and the absence of NC output. The suite inventory also requires this post to have its own tests.

On 5bdbb5fe4 the recorded suite passed 12/12 tests. The dispatcher suite passed 11/11. All nine default-machine regression tests and all 19 native tests passed. The normal CLI and an independent Rust caller reproduced the checked setup files and the matching ISO. Both duplicate exports preserved all files. Against upstream 211105042, the full plan selects 1,017 quick steps and 251 reached heavy steps. These two full gates did not run on that head.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test default_machine_missing
```

The final head 025ed4760 adds cross-post tests. The plasma suite now runs the direct Agie dispatcher and requires its native-directory refusal. The single-file smoothing test uses the same native-post predicate as the workspace. A mounted, otherwise valid Agie punch with smoothing enabled must report the setup-option error and create no directory. The existing native test checks all three default-option files against their expected bytes.

All 48 targeted checks passed on 025ed4760: seven plasma tests, seven smoothing tests, 11 native app tests, 11 dispatcher tests and 12 common recorded-stream tests. The full quick gate passed all 1,017 steps on this revision. The reached heavy gate passed all 251 steps. Both commands exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 8be1007379be77021079a648f16fc938fd56160c
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 8be1007379be77021079a648f16fc938fd56160c
```

The selector used merge base `211105042`. A separate trial merge of this head with upstream main at `36348cda6` completed without conflicts. GitHub still reported a conflict against the older base `211105042` at the time of that check.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Desktop Post dialog and receipt

The two current images show the synthetic DEMO20 punch on review revision `45d6166e1`. The picker identifies the requested finish. After posting, the receipt reports zero working steps and lists the checks and technology assignment required on the control.

| Before · Generic ISO | After · Native Agie |
| --- | --- |
| ![Earlier Generic ISO Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/before.png) | ![Current native Agie picker with requested finish](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/after.png) |

![Successful native Agie receipt with zero working steps and required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/b2756a8b79b453dfe633ac4a7c1b31443b374c1e/receipt.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: The Wire EDM desktop and script workflows can post a supported Classic Cut 2S punch as a native zero-step Agie setup directory for control review.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |
| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |
| motion: the allowance grows the material (`Guards::allowance`) | same | red |
| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

## Execution evidence

The supplied results below ran on published head `a1b186bff7e9c4f399f53828a790b383d20d87ff`, against `upstream/main` `5a77703b5`.
The [author evidence](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2890#issuecomment-7071668518) records these results.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 398 steps, 0 failed (54.1 min).
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green, 239 steps, 0 failed (47.4 min).
  Selected lanes: `motion heavy: every target` and `app heavy: every target`.
  All six expected-failure probes (#1950, #2849) failed as expected.

The latest refresh merged `upstream/main` without conflicts.

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
## What changed

It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.
Two legacy-extent tests generate box burns and check the corner gouges.

The undercut stock check uses exact disc-polygon intersection.
It blocks a plunge or retract when the cutter head meets a stock corner.
The lollipop profile draws the full ball united with the neck.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.
The correct finish electrode then failed the extent check.
The original pin reported a burned X extent of `19.962` for a `20.000` cavity.

## Tests

Each mutation failed its pin with the old code or the guard removed.
Each pin passed after restoration:

- `old-generator`: red / green.
- `shape-point-limit`: red / green.
- `region-lattice`: red / green.
- `extentmatch`: red / green.

## Refresh and validation

PR #2714 merged at `c9410977a`. This PR no longer requires a stack.

Author checks on `38f484aea`:

- Remove both new outline clears: both pins RED at generation. Restore: seven suite tests GREEN.

## Not exercised

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_slot_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

- `face_contour_and_slot_take_arc_turns_and_a_radius_through_edit_operation_and_undo`
- `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key`
- `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`
- `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp`

Two unit tests in `blend.rs`: `a_user_radius_turns_on_corner_arcs_where_the_stride_has_room` and `a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` (review fix). Two unit tests there changed with the plan type (`bool` became `Option<Turn>`).

Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the motion pin does not compile, because `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` and `SlotParams` have no such fields (`error[E0560]`).

Mutation results. Each mutation put one guard back to the old behaviour. Each pin went red, and green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Contour reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Contour has no radius door | `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Face does not read `blend_radius` | `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Face has no radius door | `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off` | red |
| Face step goes inside the overrun line | `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line` | red |
| Face corner arcs only for rows within the tool diameter | `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool` | red |
| Slot rounds nothing | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot has no radius door | `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Slot reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot of one row says nothing | `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so` | red |
| `sane.rs` door without the three kinds | `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Face radius | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Slot option | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Contour radius | `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| Slot digest without the option | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Face digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Contour digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Slot project file drops the option on save | `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key` | red |
| Face takes the semicircle when half the spacing is less than 0.005 mm past the radius (review fix) | `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short`, `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` | red (`actual radii: [0.012500000000000178]` for 0.01 mm) |

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

Pins: `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (the reviewer's 60 x 10.025 mm case and three other spacings), and the unit test `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius`.

### Review fix: the exhaustive test literals

The latest review found missing required fields in nine exhaustive test literals from main. The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`.

- Face literals have `blend_radius: None` in `chamfer_partly_bevelled`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `setup_move_order`, `stock_copy_hole`, `vouch_fidelity` and `vouch_fidelity_mcp`.
- Slot literals have `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in `tilt_basis0_edited_file` and `tilt_stock_cap`.
- Current main adds the same missing Face default in `first_traverse_mill_turn` and `model_fidelity_wide`. These literals have `blend_radius: None` too.

- Current main also adds a Contour literal and a Slot literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`. The Contour literal has `blend_radius: None`. The Slot literal has `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None`.

- The test helper in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` also has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`.

- The Contour literal in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs` has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `equal_steps::edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`.

The fix adds 18 default-field lines in fourteen files. All changed literals are in tests. It changes no runtime source logic.

Runtime pins: eleven app suites passed 47 tests. Motion `equal_steps` passed 13 tests. The app first-traverse unit pin passed one test. App `equal_steps` passed six tests.

Mutation: removing the added defaults gave compiler error `E0063` in the affected literals. Restoring the defaults made all fourteen affected suites compile and pass.

Final head: `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`

Quick gate: 761 steps passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`, against upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`. The first run passed all 123 motion steps. The app build then stopped on a stale local `camcraft_kernel` artifact (`E0463`) after the check profile changed. After rebuilding that local artifact, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only app --only ui` passed all 638 selected steps, with 0 failed, in 38.6 minutes. These two runs cover the quick plan: 7,028 tests passed, 0 failed and 115 ignored. No source change was needed for the artifact failure.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`: 237 steps, 0 failed, in 44.3 minutes. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran. The lanes ran 100 passing tests and six expected failures: three for #1950 and three for #2849. There were 0 unexpected failures. Motion had 38 steps and 57 passing tests. App had 198 steps and 43 passing tests. The shared build was one step.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed in 40.41 seconds.

The results above are for the old head `4adba68fd`. The results for the current head are in the next section.

### Review fix: the merge conflicts with main

The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `6ffa808ae`. Four files had conflicts. Each resolution keeps the two sides:

- `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_projects.rs`: the Contour literals keep `blend_radius` from this PR and `chain_overrides` from main.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: `mod slot_turns;` from this PR and `mod undercut;` from main both stay.

Main added literals that do not have the new fields. These got the defaults:

- `blend_radius: None` in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`, `crates/app/tests/klartext_builtin.rs` (two literals) and `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table_tilt.rs`.
- `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in the Slot literal of `crates/app/tests/posting_rotaries_first.rs`.
- The Contour literal of this PR's `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` got `chain_overrides: Vec::new()`.

After the merge, `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs` had 402 lines, and `params_files_stay_under_the_line_law` failed. Commit `8716a45fd` moves the Face and Contour radius writes into `digest::write_blend_radius`. The digest bytes do not change. The file now has 392 lines.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

When no earlier operation cut, the stock is known. The whole pocket is cut and a note says it.

## Cause

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

## Tests

Pins, all new:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_tests.rs` (lib): `each_reading_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `a_floor_cut_at_the_cut_depth_does_not_stand_and_one_above_it_does`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_previous.rs`: 6 tests. They compare the rest area with an independent simulation of the earlier operations: a flat tool, a wall allowance, a bull-nose tool, mixed tools with a partial depth and disconnected cuts, an island. The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` now also covers the mode.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/rest_source_tests.rs`: 2 tests for the new row.

Red before the change: the pins use the new API and do not compile on `upstream/main`. Thus the mutation results below are the proof for each guard.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| every cut depth is read (`Guards::depth`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| an unreadable column stands (`Guards::unknown`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| the pocket outside the grid stands (`Guards::outside`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| one cell of growth (`Guards::cell`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| `rest_plan` refuses the new mode | `the_two_rest_modes_never_use_each_others_planner` | red | green |
| `rest_pocket_previous` refuses the entered mode | same | red | green |
| `validate` does not read the previous tool in the new mode | same | red | green |
| job: tilted plane refused | `a_tilted_plane_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_at_generation` | red | green |
| door: tilted plane refused at the edit | same | red | green |
| job: `previous_ops_refusal` is called | `a_stock_that_cannot_be_established_is_refused_by_name` | red | green |
| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |
| earlier operation stale | same | red | green |
| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |
| stamp byte 0xD8 | `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

## Review evidence on the final head

The final head is `7969769d3f98555fab3448d5936214f91cb0736f`.
The review requests evidence only. The source and the head stay unchanged.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` is green: 237 steps, 0 failed.
The selected lanes include every motion and app heavy target.
They ran 57 motion tests and 43 app tests. Six expected-failure probes gave the expected result.
The base is `upstream/main` at `60cb97a0b3717bf6a129e781fd8f4ec98806124b`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is red: 385 steps, 1 failed, 39.8 minutes.
Only the UI library step failed: 1373 passed, 7 failed, 7 ignored.
Six `egui_app::report_tests` tests and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds` could not create a graphics adapter.
They report `CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("No adapter found")`.
All motion and app suites passed. All selected UI integration suites passed.
App `tool_gate` passed all 9 tests, including the catalogue test that failed in the review.

`cargo clippy -j 4 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

### Before and after

These images use the existing Pocket page test fixture.
The GPU adapter was unavailable: `CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("No adapter found")`.
A temporary software renderer painted the actual egui meshes and textures.
It did not recreate the controls or their text.
The temporary capture code was removed before the final quick gate.
The three images are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.
No image or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

Before: the renderer from `upstream/main` at `60cb97a0b` uses the PR data model.
Only the default `source` field was added for model compatibility.
The source selector is absent. The three previous-tool rows are present.

![Before: previous-tool rows without the source selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ffe6b26635486bf0f5cfd5a938b6eb01d972cd51/pr-2822/before.png)

After, entered-tool mode: the new source selector and the previous-tool rows are present.

![After: entered-tool mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ffe6b26635486bf0f5cfd5a938b6eb01d972cd51/pr-2822/after-entered-tool.png)

After, previous-operations mode: the previous-tool rows are hidden. The rest allowance stays visible.

![After: previous-operations mode hides the previous-tool rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ffe6b26635486bf0f5cfd5a938b6eb01d972cd51/pr-2822/after-previous-operations.png)

The pin is `egui_app::rest_pocket_tests::source::the_source_row_switches_the_mode_hides_the_tool_rows_and_commits_on_apply`.
The pin failed when the entered-tool visibility guard was disabled.
It passed after the guard was restored.


## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup (#318). The code path is `rest::prior_state`, which the 3D Pocket uses. No test here crosses a setup boundary. The check for stale operations reads the same setup only.
- A WCS yaw. The existing `wcs_yaw::enter` turns the grid. No test here has a yaw.
- The field stock engine (#586, #637). The reader is `Columns`, which reads the two engines. The tests use the column grid.
- Zigzag and Offset rings in the new mode. They use the passes of the entered-tool mode, which has its own tests. The new tests use Waterline.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane). The new row moves the rows of a Pocket page that has rest machining on.
- The app was not started by hand. The UI tests ran the page in the test harness.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/2033-rest-previous-ops.md`)

- One rest area for all levels. An upper level can cut air where only a lower level has material.
- The strict reading keeps a band of about 1.5 cells along each wall that an earlier tool rode. The rest pass follows those walls.
- The Adaptive strategy stays refused. The Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket is retired, so `rest_adaptive` has no door from this operation.
- The MCP skill text (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`) does not describe the new `source` key. The session could not write that file. That edit is owed.
- The guide pages on the site do not describe the new mode.

## Overlaps

- #2716 changes `generate.rs`, `job.rs` and `params.rs` in other arms (the Contour kind). Different function parts. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2714 changes `generate.rs`, `params.rs` and `machining2d/mod.rs` for the Slot Undercut kind. Different lines. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2678 changes `generate.rs`, `job.rs` and `machining2d/mod.rs`. Its hunks are not in the rest branch of the Pocket arm. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: The 2D Pocket's rest machining can read the remaining material from the previous operations of the setup ("Rest stock from: Previous operations"), at every cut depth, in place of an entered previous tool.

Effort: max

Fixes #2033
